Quantifying the importance of ecosystem services in the context of agricultural carbon dioxide removal and rewetting – A deliberative choice experiment
items.summary_raw: As anthropogenic climate change progresses, the implementation of carbon dioxide removal (CDR) is being debated more frequently. This research aims to shed light on preferences for ecosystem service provision associated with agricultural CDR measures, using deliberative choice experiments with a sample of 117 German citizens. It is one of the first studies transferring deliberative monetary valuation to the online format and valuing ecosystem services in the context of agricultural CDR and rewetting. Our findings indicate that habitat for biodiversity is potentially the most highly valued ecosystem service among those evaluated. Additionally, participants considered flood protection, climate regulation and water quality to be important, while preferences for soil erosion were lower. Furthermore, individuals expressed a higher willingness to pay after being confronted with information on the potential risk of mitigation deterrence, although the underlying mechanism remains unclear.

items.title: Reactive Climate Litigation: An Analytical Framework for the Criminal Prosecution of Climate Activists
items.summary_raw: Abstract Among the various types of legal activism, a distinction can be made between proactive and reactive litigation. This distinction hinges on who initiates the legal action: proactive litigation is initiated by plaintiffs, while reactive litigation occurs when the state starts a criminal prosecution in response to activism or dissent. While proactive strategic cases have been documented, reactive criminal trials involving activists remain understudied, especially in legal scholarship. In this article, an analytical framework that mobilizes the concepts of reactive litigation and judicial opportunity is created to systematically analyze 13 criminal prosecution cases relating to climate activism. The analysis will be based on four key elements to highlight the trends that can be observed: (i) the type and targets of the protest action, (ii) the charges brought against the defendant, (iii) the defences mobilized in court, and (iv) the outcomes of the criminal proceedings. This article finds that cross-analysis of the variables across four jurisdictions not only shows the relevance of studying the prosecution of activists as a growing and pressing phenomenon around the world but also provides insight into the trends observed in reactive climate litigation.

items.title: The Development and Gaps of Integrating Climate Change Education with STEAM Education
items.summary_raw: Abstract Climate Change Education (CCE) empowers students to act on climate issues. Combining STEAM with CCE (STEAM-CCE) helps students analyse climate data and develop sustainable solutions. Although important for climate literacy under climate change, reviews on STEAM-CCE’s development and gaps are scarce. As such, this study examines STEAM-CCE in terms of (1) the spatial-temporal trend and gaps; (2) the methodological and pedagogical gaps; and (3) future research directions by reviewing 167 studies from 3 databases. Although there has been increased focus on CCE-STEAM over time, most studies do not include “Arts” in STEAM-CCE, highlighting the neglect of arts-related advocacy in enhancing climate literacy. Research is primarily focused on developed regions, such as North America and Europe, creating a geographical bias that neglects the vulnerabilities and contexts of the Global South. Pedagogically, although hands-on, project-based learning is well-established, integrating the Arts into STEAM-CCE remains a significant challenge, often superficial and failing to achieve deep transdisciplinary integration. Additionally, the review highlights critical gaps in assessment, with few formative models to evaluate complex skills, such as systems thinking and action competence, and a notable underuse of motivational strategies, including gamification and field trips. Methodologically, the field is limited by an overdependence on self-report data and a lack of longitudinal and…

items.title: Diplomacy in the digital abyss: how populism and misinformation are reshaping statecraft
items.summary_raw: A profound paradox characterizes the contemporary international system; unprecedented digital connectivity coincides with a deepening crisis of trust, creating what this paper terms a “digital abyss” for traditional diplomacy. This paper examines how populist politics and disinformation use language through framing and delegitimization to challenge traditional diplomacy and principles of statecraft. This study adopts a Constructivist theoretical approach, arguing that these forces function as a form of epistemological warfare, completely undermining the institutional legitimacy and shared realities that underpin diplomatic interaction. Findings demonstrate a fundamental shift from confidential negotiation to contested reality, challenging the possibility of international cooperation, which evades and delegitimizes international institutions. This paper concludes by proposing pathways for institutional adaptation, including cognitive immunity. By laying out a roadmap for diplomatic innovation that utilizes the conceptual and technological information landscape of 21st-century statecraft, this study advances the domains of digital diplomacy and international relations.

items.title: Canada as a clean energy ‘superpower’? Green hydrogen, between deployment and disavowal
items.summary_raw: Canada’s potential to generate more renewable energy than it needs has led to visions of it becoming a leader in low-carbon hydrogen. In the Atlantic provinces, this has involved proposals aimed at producing ‘green’ hydrogen and its derivatives, predominantly for export to Europe. Despite trade being a contributor to carbon emissions, green hydrogen offers an alternative vision where trade is used to spur a clean energy transition and decarbonize hard-to-abate industries, driving growth, jobs and investment. While critics expose the contradictions of hydrogen, they often fail to recognize the enduring appeal of trade success, materially and symbolically, linked to being a ‘clean energy superpower.’ Drawing on tensions around green ‘leadership’ and local ‘risk,’ I argue critics tend to disavow the inconsistencies of their own position, outwardly opposing green trade in Canada, while depending on, and even encouraging, green industrial production, growth and trade elsewhere.

items.title: Floods Early Warning Messages in a Rural Province in South Africa
items.summary_raw: ABSTRACT Floods remain among the most frequent and damaging natural hazards globally, with effective flood early warning messages (FEWMs) playing a critical role in reducing disaster risk and enhancing community preparedness. Despite advances in early warning systems, many rural communities in developing countries continue to experience challenges in accessing, understanding, and responding to warning information. This study assessed the effectiveness of FEWMs in the Mokgareng community of the North West Province, South Africa. A quantitative cross‐sectional survey design was adopted. Data were collected from 102 adult respondents using a structured questionnaire and analysed using descriptive statistics, a Generalised Linear Mixed Model (GLMM), and binary logistic regression in R Statistical Software. The findings revealed a substantial gap between awareness and exposure to FEWMs. Although most respondents reported understanding the meaning of FEWMs and expressed confidence in interpreting warning information, many indicated that they had not received or could not recall receiving warning messages. High levels of cellphone ownership suggest strong potential for mobile‐based dissemination; however, significant concerns were identified regarding message reach, community consultation, and dissemination pathways. items.title: Beyond consensus: Negotiating climate citizenship through deliberative communication in school-based climate action
items.summary_raw: This study critically examines deliberative democracy within school-based climate action, contending that student agency and participation in climate citizenship education are shaped by communicative processes rather than solely by individual capability. While environmental education increasingly addresses climate change, instrumental and technocratic approaches continue to restrict authentic democratic engagement. Employing a critical ethnographic methodology informed by Habermasian communicative action and Freirean critical pedagogy, data were collected from a school-based climate action programme involving teachers, students, and external facilitators. The findings indicate that deliberative processes are shaped by communicative, instrumental, and strategic rationalities, resulting in asymmetrical negotiation, partial compromise, and contingent consensus. Although dialogic spaces foster student participation and critical reflection, these opportunities are constrained by institutional structures, cultural norms, and power relations. The study concludes that student agency is context-dependent and relational, emerging from communicative processes. It recommends repositioning climate education as a dialogic and participatory space to more effectively support democratic engagement.

items.title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Climate Change Mitigation in Africa: A Sustainable Approach
items.source_name: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
items.summary_raw: As climate change intensifies environmental and socio-economic vulnerabilities across Africa, there is a growing need for innovative, scalable solutions to support climate resilience. This study critically examines the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in enhancing climate adaptation and mitigation efforts on the continent. Employing a qualitative, multi-source research methodology, the paper synthesizes academic literature, institutional frameworks, and applied case studies to assess the integration of AI into environmental monitoring and resource management systems. Particular emphasis is placed on the use of machine learning and remote sensing technologies to support real-time data analysis, land-use classification, water resource management, and early warning systems. The Enhancing National Climate Services (ENACTS) program is analyzed as a leading case, demonstrating how the fusion of satellite and groundbased data can significantly improve climate services in sectors such as agriculture and public health. The paper also identifies critical challenges—including data scarcity, inadequate infrastructure, limited technical capacity, and ethical risks such as data privacy and algorithmic bias—that hinder the effective deployment of AI. In response, the study offers strategic policy recommendations to strengthen climate data infrastructure, promote cross-sector collaboration, and build human capital in AI and climate science. The findings underscore the importance of…

items.title: Navigating the low-altitude economy: stakeholder perceptions and ecosystem implications of UAM in China
items.summary_raw: Abstract Urban Air Mobility (UAM), particularly passenger-oriented electric vertical take-off and landing services, is increasingly promoted as part of future urban transport, but its adoption depends on coordination among regulators, engineers, operators, investors and researchers. This study develops an ecosystem-oriented framework integrating socio-technical transition theory, innovation ecosystem theory and a flying electric Mobility-as-a-Service perspective. A PESTLE-based survey of 149 stakeholders in Jiangsu Province, China, was analysed using K-modes clustering and exploratory factor analysis. The results show limited baseline familiarity with UAM and substantial heterogeneity in perceived drivers and barriers. Four attitudinal profiles were identified: proactive supporters, highly cautious stakeholders, policy-trusting stakeholders and technologically neutral stakeholders. Factor analysis revealed four underlying dimensions: technological performance and system safety, policy guidance and economic incentives, public acceptance and market awareness, and environmental sustainability. Stakeholder roles were associated with different priorities, with governance actors placing greater emphasis on policy support and technical stakeholders expressing stronger implementation concerns. The findings indicate that scalable UAM deployment requires predictable governance, transparent safety assurance, evidence-based decision support and user-centred service integration. This…

items.title: Feedback Loops in Practice: A Case Study on Evaluating a Climate Collaborative
items.summary_raw: Philanthropic support to address the climate crisis has grown substantially, yet it remains unclear how effectively philanthropies are learning from their investments, from each other, and from other actors about what generates meaningful impact. Evaluations have come under scrutiny, as conventional approaches often struggle to account for complexity and provide the timely insights needed for adaptive management. In this article, the authors present the learning journey of a complex, systems-focused climate philanthropy initiative that uses structured feedback loops as an evaluation design. They describe how these loops were implemented over a two-year evaluation; discuss the choice of complexity-aware methods; and analyze the relational and power dynamics navigated by the funder, regrantor, and evaluation team. The authors also reflect critically on elements that received insufficient attention, particularly the learning priorities of grantees and the implications of these gaps for collaborative learning. They conclude by offering a Three Horizons framing to outline pathways for the philanthropic collaborative to strengthen its learning practice.

items.title: How narrative climate messages influence behavioral intentions and policy acceptance: the role of anxiety and fear
items.source_name: International Journal of Sustainable Development & World Ecology
items.summary_raw: Climate change communication should move beyond the mere provision of scientific information and incorporate approaches, such as narrative, that can elicit emotional responses. This study examined whether presenting climate change information in a narrative rather than an expository format influences behavioral intention and policy acceptance through specific emotions, namely anxiety and fear. An online randomized experiment was conducted in Japan with 2,121 adults. Participants received comparable information about the impacts of climate change in either a narrative format featuring a future character or an expository format presenting the same content in a logical structure. Analyses were restricted to 908 respondents who passed an attention check. The narrative condition elicited significantly stronger emotion than the expository condition. Mediation analyses showed significant indirect effects of information format on both behavioral intention and policy acceptance through emotion, whereas the direct effects were no longer statistically significant after emotion was included in the models. These findings suggest that narrative climate messages may influence behavioral intention and policy acceptance primarily by increasing emotional engagement rather than through a direct persuasive effect. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of considering emotional engagement when designing climate change communication.

items.title: Governance-by-signifier and the far-right politics of “woke” in the European Parliament
items.summary_raw: Abstract Far-right actors in the European Parliament increasingly use “woke” as a catch-all term for very different political conflicts. Debates over gender, migration and climate are often folded into a single story about ideological excess and unwanted interference from Brussels. This article develops the concept of governance-by-signifier to explain how that process works. It identifies three mechanisms: condensation, through which distinct issues are presented as part of the same threat; transposition, through which arguments move from one policy area to another; and authorisation, through which restrictive positions are normalised. The analysis draws on 85 parliamentary and para-parliamentary texts linked to the European Conservatives and Reformists and Patriots for Europe. The two groups speak in noticeably different registers. PfE relies more heavily on confrontation, civilisational threat and promises of restoration, while ECR tends to express similar concerns through the language of competence, subsidiarity and proportionality. Yet these differences often lead in the same direction. Both groups use anti-woke discourse to question rights claims, resist supranational authority and portray the above-mentioned policy areas as ideological overreach. The article shows how loose political labels can travel across policy areas and acquire real institutional force.

items.title: Optimizing Hybrid SMR–Renewable Energy Systems for Remote and Climate-Vulnerable Communities: A Techno-Economic Framework
items.summary_raw: Remote and climate-vulnerable northern communities in Canada remain heavily dependent on diesel-based electricity and heating, leading to high energy costs, fuel-supply challenges, and significant greenhouse gas emissions. This study develops a techno-economic framework to evaluate hybrid small modular reactor (SMR)-renewable energy systems for remote regions. The framework integrates a 6 MW light-water SMR, wind and photovoltaic (PV) generation, battery energy storage, combined heat and power (CHP) recovery, and hydrogen production from surplus electricity. A representative cluster of northern Canadian communities is used as a case study, and two hybrid system configurations are assessed. The SMR-wind-battery configuration achieves the best economic performance, with a levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) of $0.26/kWh and a net present cost (NPC) of $241 million, compared with $0.31/kWh and $288 million for the SMR-wind-PV-battery configuration. A diesel-only reference system yields an LCOE of $0.72/kWh and an NPC of $675 million. In both optimized configurations, the SMR supplies 52.5 GWh/year of electricity, representing 75-78% of total generation, and provides about 96 GWh th /year of recoverable thermal energy through CHP operation. Surplus electricity supports hydrogen production of approximately 215,000-261,000 kg/year. Sensitivity and Monte Carlo analyses identify SMR capital cost as the dominant source of economic uncertainty, followed by battery and wind-turbine…

items.title: The Red Thaw: Soviet climate science and the politics of global warming, 1950s–1991
items.source_name: The British Journal for the History of Science
items.summary_raw: Abstract This article examines how climate science developed in the Soviet Union from the 1950s to the early 1990s as a field shaped both by international scientific exchange and by the political priorities of the Soviet state. Focusing on the climatologist Mikhail Budyko and his research group at the State Hydrological Institute in Leningrad, it shows how Soviet scientists participated actively in emerging international discussions of anthropogenic climate change while working within institutions shaped by the priorities of socialist planning. Soviet climatologists were among the early contributors to the scientific analysis of global warming, yet they often interpreted its implications differently from their Western counterparts. In the USSR, warming was understood less as an environmental crisis than as a process compatible with long-term planning, technological intervention and, in some regions, potential economic benefit. Drawing on archival materials and interviews, the article traces how climate knowledge circulated between domestic and international scientific arenas while remaining shaped by the political culture of the late Soviet state. The Soviet case challenges narratives that explain political inaction on climate primarily through ignorance or denial, showing instead how the political significance of climate knowledge depended on the institutional frameworks through which it was interpreted and mobilized.

items.title: Institutional Trust, Affordability, and Willingness to Pay for Climate Policy
items.source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.summary_raw: Abstract Public support is central to the political feasibility of climate mitigation, yet the willingness to bear its financial costs may depend on factors beyond climate concern. Using the 2010 and 2023 waves of the Life in Transition Survey in 25 post-socialist countries, we examine how institutional trust and household expenditure are associated with willingness to pay (WTP), understood as giving part of one's income or paying higher taxes to combat climate change. Drawing on a stylized choice model in which this decision depends on the valuation of climate outcomes, the affordability of contributions, and the credibility of the institutions expected to use them, we estimate linear probability models with wave interactions and compare EU, post-Soviet, Baltic, and Balkan country groups. Both trust and expenditure are positively associated with WTP, but their relative importance shifted over time. Between 2010 and 2023, the income effect weakened while the trust effect strengthened, mainly in the post-Soviet, Baltic, and Balkan countries and much less in the EU group. These findings are robust to allowing the effect of climate concern to vary between waves and to logit estimation. Climate concern is strongly associated with WTP, yet concern alone does not ensure support for costly climate action. The political feasibility of financing mitigation also depends on institutional credibility and on public confidence that contributions will be used effectively, transparently…

items.title: Temperature testing Brexit – the case of Northern Ireland
items.summary_raw: As the only regular polling of the views of Northern Ireland's voters on Brexit, the Testing the Temperature polls (2021–2026) provide important insights into how opinions have evolved over time and in response to key developments. We provide here an analysis of the poll findings concerning attitudes towards the particular arrangements put in place by UK-EU agreement to manage the effects of Brexit on Northern Ireland, namely the Protocol on Ireland/Northern Ireland (since 2023, ‘the Windsor Framework’) and trust in those with responsibility for implementing it. This data reveals the degree to which existing political differences in Northern Ireland have been deepened post-Brexit, not only between political groupings but within them, specifically between hardline and more moderate unionists. Ultimately this study shows that opinion on Brexit-related matters is especially entrenched and slow to change in Northern Ireland, partly because it is a matter of principle for some and partly because the handling of Brexit has contributed to a decline in public confidence in political institutions and parties.

items.title: Exploring stakeholders’ perspective on climate declaration and the use of timber as a structural material in the Swedish construction industry
items.summary_raw: By 2050, the European Union aims to achieve climate-neutrality; Sweden is even aiming to achieve this goal by 2045. In this decarbonization process, the construction industry and notably the construction and production stage account for a large share of emissions. To raise awareness and decrease emissions, Sweden has introduced legislation requiring climate declarations for buildings. This is currently limited to construction and production stage. Although these efforts have been made and timber has the potential to be a low-emission structural material, its use in buildings of all types, except single-family houses, is limited. The construction industry includes many different stakeholders and there is a limited understanding of how they view climate declarations as well as barriers to and drivers for increasing the use of timber as a structural material. This study investigated the perspectives of stakeholders with a variety of stakeholder and organizational characteristics. To reduce the environmental impacts of this sector, the stakeholders highlighted the importance of the climate declaration law and the need for binding requirements. However, to increase the use of timber as a low-emission structural material, “inertia” and “technical risks associated with timber buildings” were the most significant barriers from stakeholders’ perspective. While educational programs offered by the organization were identified as an important factor in overcoming barriers. In addition…

items.title: Simulation of the medium- and long-term development of China's hydrogen energy industry and policy impacts
items.summary_raw: China's hydrogen supply structure remains heavily dependent on fossil fuels, making the promotion of green and low-carbon development in the hydrogen energy industry (HEI) critical for achieving national dual-carbon targets. This study forecasts future trends in China's HEI and explores policy pathways to support its sustainable development. To this end, a system dynamics (SD) model is developed to analyze the medium- and long-term development of China's HEI. The model captures hydrogen production from both fossil-based and renewable sources, while also accounting for carbon emissions from the gray hydrogen sector, and systematically evaluates the impacts of relevant policy interventions. The results indicate that: (1) Under the current development trajectory, green hydrogen production is projected to reach 7.5335 million tonnes (Mt) by 2035, with alkaline water electrolysis remaining the dominant technology. (2) In the absence of policy constraints, gray hydrogen production is expected to peak at 34.5072 Mt in 2034, with associated carbon emissions of 678.2689 Mt, and coal-based hydrogen remaining the primary source. (3) Unit subsidies for green hydrogen, tax incentives, and capacity replacement policies are more effective in promoting green hydrogen development than fixed asset investment subsidies and technological progress alone. (4) Capacity replacement and reduction policies accelerate the timing of peak fossil-based hydrogen production and reduce peak levels, while…

items.title: Rethinking Small State Paradigm: Nuclear Pragmatism in Slovakia under the European Green Deal
items.summary_raw: This article argues that the binary of compliance versus resistance does not explain Slovakia’s behaviour, but domestic economic structures, technological capabilities, and geopolitical vulnerabilities characterise its adaptation to European Union (EU) climate commitments. It synthesises small state and securitisation theories, and the empirical findings drawn upon semi-structured elite interviews with representatives from Slovak government institutions, European organisations, industry associations, trade unions, think tanks, and academia show that the 2022 Russian attack on Ukraine has heightened a securitised understanding of climate governance in Slovakia. In this context, the concepts of resilience, energy security, competitiveness, and decarbonisation come to the forefront. The results also indicate that nuclear energy is not only seen as a low-carbon technology and an energy-security instrument but also as a strategic asset, which supports cooperation in the context of EU climate governance, diversification of suppliers, technological continuity, and industrial competitiveness. Thus, nuclear pragmatism emerges as a preference of Slovakia. The article also adds to the debates about the European integration process, EU climate governance, energy security, and the potential for small states.

items.title: Effectiveness of Education on Global Climate Change and Environmental Health Using Crossword Puzzles in Nursing Students
items.summary_raw: The aim of this study was to investigate the effectiveness of educating nursing students on global climate change awareness and environmental attitude levels using crossword puzzles. This one-group pretest-posttest quasi-experimental study was conducted between February 2024 and June 2024 with 302 nursing undergraduate students in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th grades at a nursing school in the Western Black Sea Region of Türkiye. A six-session face-to-face education program with a crossword puzzle on global climate change and environmental health was implemented for nursing students. Data collection tools consisted of “Introductory Information Form”, “University Students' Awareness Scale on Global Climate Change” and “Environmental Attitude Scale” and were applied before and after the education. Descriptive statistics and dependent sample t-test were used to evaluate the data. The mean posttest score of the students’ global climate change awareness level (2.68±0.35) was significantly higher than the mean pre-test score (2.18±0.31) (p=0.000). Similarly, the mean post-test score of nursing students’ environmental attitude (65.91±8.34) was significantly higher than the mean pre-test score (59.16±5.13) (p=0.000). The education given to nursing students with crossword puzzles as one of the innovative learning techniques was effective in increasing their global climate change awareness and environmental attitude levels.

items.title: Beyond the single story: intersectional framing of poverty and climate change in Arabic YouTube Videos
items.summary_raw: This study examines the intersectional framing of poverty and climate change in Arabic YouTube videos, addressing a critical gap in media research on underrepresented regions. Using multimodal framing, it analyzes 277 videos to examine how visual, verbal (spoken transcripts), textual (video titles and hashtags), and emotional elements shape narratives around these interconnected issues. Arab media predominantly employ vulnerability, climate justice, and economic effects frames, emphasizing climate change’s disproportionate impact on marginalized communities and developing countries while attributing responsibility to industrialized countries. Visual framing relies heavily on scientific data graphics and images of drought and water scarcity; emotional framing is dominated by fear, followed by hope and anger. The findings underscore top-down climate communication in the Arab region, with limited grassroots and empowerment narratives, and call for inclusive, human-centered narratives that amplify local voices and public engagement.

items.title: Green Port Transformation in Renewable Energy and Sustainable Water Port Management: Strategies for Climate-Resilient Maritime Infrastructure
items.summary_raw: Ports play a critical role in global trade infrastructure, however they are also a significant source of GHG emissions, energy use as well as marine environmental damage. The shift towards “green ports” has become a strategy to lessen the ecological footprint and enhance the efficiency of port operations by incorporating renewable energy sources, sustainable water management, and climate-resilient infrastructure. The role of traditional ports in becoming sustainable, maritime hubs will be discussed and the implementation of renewable energy technologies, including solar photovoltaic (PV) systems, offshore wind, shore-side electricity and clean energy storage, will be outlined. Furthermore, it examines the management of water port in sustainable use of wastewater treatment, ballast water control, rain water harvesting, desalination technologies, as well as protection of marine ecosystems. The study pinpoints technological innovations, policy frameworks and management approaches to developing a low carbon port. The study examines global green port initiatives and sustainable practices to gain insights into the challenges and opportunities of implementing sustainable port operations. Results highlight the need for holistic approaches to energy and water-use management for creating resilient ports to support sustainable shipping and sustainable goals.

items.title: The Senate’s Big Bipartisan Permitting Deal, Explained
items.summary_raw: It’s taken two presidential administrations, four years, and who-knows-how-many proposals that never saw the light of the Senate floor. But a long-awaited bipartisan deal to streamline the country’s permitting system is here. On Tuesday, a bipartisan gang of senators — the leaders of the Environment and Public Works and Energy and Natural Resources committees — released an omnibus legislative package meant to streamline many permitting processes across the country. Dubbing themselves the “Four Corners,” the lawmakers — Shelley Moore Capito of West Virginia, Martin Heinrich of New Mexico, Mike Lee of Utah, and Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island — framed the deal as a way to lower energy costs, stabilize the energy system, and expand the economy. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act , or BAAJA, aims to address a wide-ranging set of complaints that lawmakers have about the energy and permitting system. It would streamline the often arduous permitting processes that can ensnarl and delay virtually any kind of federal infrastructure project, rewriting a slew of largely procedural laws that have come to frustrate leaders in both parties. And it would limit executive agencies from hemming specific sectors of the energy industry, as President Donald Trump has done to the wind sector and previous Democratic presidents did to oil and gas. The bill would also encourage a build-out of new long-distance power lines, which could help calm surging power prices and unlock more…

items.title: Targeted extracellular degradation of LRP8 promotes ferroptosis in cancer cells
items.summary_raw: Tumor reliance on antioxidant defenses creates a vulnerability to ferroptosis, yet strategies to therapeutically disable these systems remain limited. Here, we identify targeted degradation of the selenium uptake receptor lipoprotein receptor-related protein 8 (LRP8) as an effective approach to decrease the abundance of the ferroptosis-protective enzyme glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4). Using bispecific cytokine receptor–targeting chimeras (KineTACs) that couple LRP8 to cytokine receptor internalization pathways, we selectively direct LRP8 to the lysosome for degradation. LRP8 degradation reduces the abundance of several selenoproteins, including GPX4, lowering the cellular threshold for lipid peroxidation and sensitizing cancer cells to ferroptosis. These findings establish receptor-mediated selenium uptake as a critical, targetable node in ferroptosis resistance and demonstrate that extracellular protein degradation can be leveraged to reprogram intracellular translational dependencies in cancer cells. More broadly, this work provides a framework for exploiting nutrient acquisition pathways to overcome therapy resistance.

items.title: Passive sampling for grazer cues incorporates top-down effects in harmful algal bloom monitoring and toxin prediction
items.summary_raw: Domoic acid (DA) produced by toxigenic species of the diatom genus Pseudo-nitzschia during harmful algal blooms (HABs) bioaccumulates in filter feeders, bait fish, and commercial seafood products, posing a threat to marine organisms and public health. Copepodamides, a group of polar lipids exuded by copepods, are known to induce DA production in multiple species of Pseudo-nitzschia . However, copepodamides are not currently considered in HAB monitoring and prediction, in part because of challenges associated with measuring ambient concentrations of dilute and labile compounds. Here we employ solid phase adsorption toxin tracking (SPATT) to measure natural concentrations of copepodamides over 28 mo in Monterey Bay, California, a known hotspot for HAB events. Copepodamides were significantly correlated to copepod biovolume, confirming utility as a zooplankton proxy. In generalized linear models, copepodamides from SPATT provided greater accuracy and lead time for predicting Pseudo-nitzschia abundance and DA concentration in sentinel mussels than DA from SPATT. Field experiments in the Northeast Atlantic assessed sampling methodology, and lab experiments demonstrated DA induction in Pseudo-nitzschia multiseries isolated from Monterey Bay. Results show potential for copepodamides to improve HAB predictions and encourage development of novel approaches to include top-down information in HAB monitoring systems.

items.title: A highly potent bispecific antibody confers complete protection against SFTSV in preclinical models
items.summary_raw: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) is an emerging bunyavirus that causes severe human disease, with a case fatality rate of up to 30%. However, no licensed therapeutics are currently available for clinical use. Here, we identified two SFTSV neutralizing nanobodies (Nbs), N2C1 and N2D2, which inhibited both viral attachment and membrane fusion. Structural analysis revealed that N2C1 spanned Gn domain I and domain III, while N2D2 targeted domain I, located at the inner and outer sides of the Gn–Gc hexamer crown, respectively. They also exhibited synergistic neutralization, and their bispecific antibody (bsAb) displayed dramatically enhanced neutralizing potency. In a lethal mouse model, the bsAb demonstrated superior protective efficacy over the parental Nbs in both preexposure and postexposure administration regimens. More importantly, in preclinical ferret models, the bsAb N2D2-Fc-N2C1 conferred complete protection against SFTSV not only at a low dose of 5 mg/kg but also when administered as late as 2 d postinfection. These results demonstrate the potent protective efficacy of N2D2-Fc-N2C1, supporting its development as a promising clinical candidate against SFTSV infection.

items.title: Atg39-dependent nucleophagy and Atg40-dependent ER-phagy require the Apq12/Brr6/Brl1 complex
items.summary_raw: Autophagic degradation of parts of the nucleus (nucleophagy) and endoplasmic reticulum (ER-phagy) utilizes the selective autophagy receptors, Atg39 and Atg40, that link their target structures to the autophagy machinery. Here, we show that a complex of three proteins, Apq12, Brr6, and Brl1, is needed for both Atg39-dependent nucleophagy and Atg40-dependent ER-phagy. Apq12, Brr6, and Brl1 each have two transmembrane domains flanking a luminal region that contains an amphipathic helix. The Apq12/Brr6/Brl1 complex has been implicated in membrane remodeling during nuclear pore formation. While autophagosomal flux is unaffected by the loss of Apq12, Brr6, or Brl1, vacuolar delivery of outer and inner nuclear membrane proteins (Hmg1, Nvj1, and Src1), pan-ER proteins (Sec63 and Per33), and an ER tubule junction protein (Lnp1) is blocked. In apq12Δ cells, Atg39 and Atg40 receptors concentrate in puncta and associate with the autophagic machinery; however, their delivery to the vacuole is blocked. Atg39 puncta extend into the cytoplasm but fail to detach from the nuclear envelope (NE), suggesting a defect in membrane scission. Coimmunoprecipitation and crosslinking analysis indicate that Atg39 and Atg40 interact with the Apq12/Brr6/Brl1 complex. We propose that the membrane remodeling activity of the Apq12/Brr6/Brl1 complex is needed to release fragments of the NE and ER so they can be sequestered within autophagosomes for degradation.

items.title: A conserved β-sheet motif mediates PIN2 hydrophilic loop–loop interactions to regulate PIN2 dynamics
items.summary_raw: PIN-FORMED (PIN) auxin transporters are essential for plant development, relying on asymmetric localization at the plasma membrane. While the central hydrophilic loop (HL) of PINs is known to integrate various regulatory signals, the structural basis of its coordination remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that the PIN–HL domain undergoes homotypic interaction independent of the transmembrane domains via a conserved β-sheet motif. Deleting this motif in PIN2 reinforced protein clustering and polarity, and impaired intracellular trafficking, leading to defective root gravitropism. These phenotypes were successfully reversed through rapamycin-induced reconstitution of the HL–HL interaction, confirming that this physical association is vital for native PIN2 behavior. Furthermore, we show that phosphorylation of the HL domain inhibits this interaction, which in turn modulates the recruitment of PIN-regulatory factors. Our findings support a model in which the HL–HL interaction serves as a regulatory hub, where phosphorylation and other modulators converge to influence PIN behavior.

items.title: Ufd4p-mediated Sum1p clearance ensures proper chromosome organization during cell division
items.summary_raw: Chromosome architecture is essential for faithful chromosome segregation and genome stability. However, the mechanisms underlying chromosome organization are not well-characterized. Here, we identify the ubiquitin ligase Ufd4p as a master regulator of chromosome organization. Ufd4p deficiency causes longer chromosome axes and increased meiotic crossovers due to compromised condensation. Multiomics profiling reveals that Ufd4p promotes transcription of condensin components required for chromosome condensation. Mechanistically, Ufd4p targets Sum1p, a subunit of histone deacetylase complex, for proteasomal degradation. Sum1p accumulation reduces histone 4 lysine 5 acetylation, thereby suppressing condensin transcription and ultimately leading to chromosome condensation defects. Intriguingly, this pathway is shared in both meiosis and mitosis. Moreover, the mammalian homolog TRIP12 effectively rescues chromosome organization defects in ufd4 mutants, suggesting an evolutionarily conserved mechanism. Collectively, our study elucidates an evolutionarily conserved ubiquitin–proteasome system (UPS)-dependent mechanism controlling the proper chromosome organization, highlighting the pivotal role of UPS in regulating chromosome architecture across species.

items.title: Genome stability disrupted by the circRBM39(4,5,6)–RPA2 axis represses breast tumorigenesis
items.summary_raw: Genome instability (GI) is a hallmark of cancer. GI is associated with accumulative DNA damage and tumor-specific defects in DNA repair. Multiple antitumor drugs have been developed to promote persistent GI and to drive DNA damage beyond a threshold that tumor cells can survive. However, regulatory roles of circular RNAs (circRNAs) in GI and DNA damage remain elusive. Through circRNA profiling and a small interfering RNA (siRNA)-mediated screen, we have identified a circRNA termed circRBM39(4,5,6) , which is significantly decreased in breast cancer (BC) and disrupts DNA damage response. CircRBM39(4,5,6) inhibits breast tumorigenesis through increasing DNA damage and promoting sensitivity to the antitumor drug poly Adenosine Diphosphate (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor (PARPi). Mechanistically, cytoplasmic circRBM39(4,5,6) interacts with replication protein A2 (RPA2), an essential DNA repair factor, through a 7-nt AG-rich motif and destabilizes RPA2 protein by facilitating HECT and RCC1-like domain 2 (HERC2)-mediated ubiquitination, thus repressing homologous recombination repair. Importantly, administration of in vitro synthesized circRBM39(4,5,6) substantially inhibits breast tumorigenesis, sensitizes BC cells to PARPi, and renders them susceptible to synthetic lethality (SL) in distinct breast tumorigenesis mouse models. Our findings highlight the interplay between circRNA and GI in cancers, and the SL of circRBM39(4,5,6) to PARPi provides strategies for RNA-based BC…

items.title: Mathematical discovery and exploration can be done at scale
items.summary_raw: AlphaEvolve, introduced in A. Novikov et al . [“AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery” (Tech. Rep., Google DeepMind, 2025).], is a generic evolutionary coding agent that combines large language models (LLMs) with automated evaluation in a loop that proposes, tests, and refines algorithmic solutions. Here we showcase AlphaEvolve as a tool for autonomously discovering novel mathematical constructions and making progress on long-standing open problems. On 67 problems spanning mathematical analysis, combinatorics, geometry, and number theory, the system rediscovered the best known solutions in most cases and improved on them in several. In some instances, it also generalized results for finitely many input values into a formula valid for all inputs. Furthermore, we combine this methodology with Deep Think [Google DeepMind, Advanced Version of Gemini with Deep Think Officially Achieves Gold-Medal Standard at the International Mathematical Olympiad (Google DeepMind Blog, 2025).] and AlphaProof [Google DeepMind, AI Achieves Silver-Medal Standard Solving International Mathematical Olympiad Problems (Google DeepMind Blog, 2024).] in a broader framework where the additional proof assistants and reasoning systems provide automated proof generation and further mathematical insights. These results demonstrate that LLM-guided evolutionary search can autonomously discover mathematical constructions that complement human intuition, at times matching or…

items.title: Scaling laws for massively parallel microfluidics enable rapid construction of ten-million-scale natively paired antibody libraries
items.summary_raw: Droplet microfluidics enables compartmentalized single-cell analysis, but conventional single-nozzle systems cannot efficiently process millions of cells needed to identify rare populations. This bottleneck is particularly important in antibody discovery, which requires deep B cell sampling while preserving the native pairing of antibody heavy and light chains. Parallelization increases throughput, but cumulative pressure losses cause flow nonuniformity across large networks. Here, we establish an exact hydrodynamic model for ladder-geometry networks and demonstrate that the maximum flow deviation scales quadratically with the number of parallel units [ O ( N 2 )] rather than linearly [ O ( N )]. Computational fluid dynamics simulations for representative network geometries validate this scaling law. We extend it to hierarchical ( A × B ) networks and implement the resulting rules in a computational tool for forward evaluation and inverse channel design. Guided by this framework, we develop 100- and 360-generator chips that increase droplet generation rates by up to 53.8-fold while maintaining stable dripping, low droplet-size variation (CV ≤ 13.8%), and low mean cell occupancy (λ ≤ 0.02). Using a two-stage workflow, we construct natively paired antibody libraries from 1 million primary human B cells, achieving a 14-fold reduction in expensive reagent consumption relative to conventional methods. We further validate the encapsulation of 10 million cells within 40 min…

items.title: The circSNX6 restricts dengue virus replication in association with PARP1 and ferroptosis
items.summary_raw: Dengue virus (DENV) infection poses a persistent global health challenge with no specific antiviral therapy. Although circular RNAs (circRNAs) regulate antiviral immunity, their roles in DENV infection remain largely unexplored. Here, transcriptome sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from dengue patients across disease phases and severities identified 15 circRNAs consistently dysregulated across all clinical stages, enriched in ferroptosis, glutathione metabolism, and endocytosis pathways. Among these, hsa_circ_0031607 (circSNX6) was the sole circRNA linked to all three pathways and was upregulated in both dengue patients and DENV2-infected human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). circSNX6 overexpression suppressed DENV2 replication, whereas its knockdown enhanced viral propagation. Mechanistically, circSNX6 localized to the cytoplasm and interacted with PARP1. DENV2 infection induced partial PARP1 redistribution from nucleus to cytoplasm. circSNX6 suppressed PARP1 expression; its knockdown increased global PARylation, accompanied by enhanced NRF2 PARylation and altered TFR1 and GPX4 expression. In cultured cells, ferrostatin-1 reduced and erastin enhanced DENV2 replication; olaparib or ferrostatin-1 partially attenuated the proviral effects of circSNX6 knockdown, while erastin partially reversed the antiviral effect of circSNX6 overexpression. In mice, olaparib reduced serum and hepatic viral loads and attenuated hepatic pathology; ferrostatin-1…

Tandem RNA-binding domain architecture drives PKR activation through an intramolecular interface
items.summary_raw: Tandem repeats of RNA-binding domains (RBDs), often linked by intrinsically disordered sequences, are prevalent among RNA-binding proteins (RBPs). The inherent flexibility of these arrangements, however, raises the question of whether such domains can adopt defined configurations critical for function. Here, we reveal that in Protein Kinase R (PKR)—an RBP that triggers the innate immune response upon sensing double-stranded RNAs (dsRNAs)—its two dsRNA-binding domains (dsRBDs) assemble into a unique architecture through intramolecular interactions. This dsRBD1:dsRBD2 interface allows PKR to convert diffusive, transient contacts with RNA into a stabilized complex on the duplex, establishing a scaffold required for downstream protein dimerization and phosphorylation. Disrupting this dsRBD1:dsRBD2 interface dismantles the tandem dsRBD architecture and severely impairs PKR activity both in vitro and in cells. Together, these findings uncover an exceptional advantage of the tandem dsRBD arrangement and underscore intramolecular RBD coupling as a mechanism for regulating RBP activity.

items.title: Deep-earth water transport beyond the transition zone via subducted feldspars
items.summary_raw: Subducted potassium feldspar transforms into a hollandite-type structure, rendering it a plausible carrier for large lithophile elements and volatiles, possibly including molecular water, into the deep mantle. Nevertheless, the capacity of this phase to incorporate and retain such incompatible species under deeper mantle conditions has remained largely unconstrained. We report here the formation of the hydrated hollandite-type structures from subducting K-bearing feldspars in the presence of H 2 O near 400 km depth conditions. Combined in situ high-pressure and -temperature synchrotron X-ray diffraction and ex situ synchrotron Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy reveal molecular H 2 O incorporated within the expanded 1D tunnels together with hydroxyls through the aluminosilicate octahedral framework of the hollandite-type structure, yielding up to net ~1.97 wt.% water content. Subsequently, dehydration occurs via framework distortion upon exceeding the lower boundary of the mantle transition zone near 720 to 780 km. We estimate that, over a 200 Ma of subduction cycle, hydrated hollandite-type phases may have contributed the water flux to the topmost lower mantle by the amount to suppress the formation of the representative lower mantle phase, bridgmanite. This process may thus be linked to the apparent depression of 660-km discontinuity in penetrating slabs and their surrounding regions to address key limitations of existing akimotoite- and basalt-derived models.

items.title: Metabolite ratiomics: Rapid diagnosis and classification of gliomas for intraoperative application during brain surgery
items.summary_raw: Gliomas are diffusely infiltrative, requiring accurate and sensitive diagnostic tools during surgical resection. Mutations in isocitrate dehydrogenase enzyme (IDH) alter its normal activity and result in accumulation of a unique oncometabolite, 2-hydroxyglutarate (2HG), in tumor cells. However, IDH-wild-type (IDH-wt) gliomas are more common and typically more aggressive. Here, 86 human brain samples were analyzed by syringe touch spray mass spectrometry to evaluate molecular alterations in gliomas. Tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) experiments were performed to minimize isobaric and isomeric interferences, and a ratiometric approach (using only signals for endogenous compounds) was employed to improve reliability of the measurements. Multiple ratios for pairs of metabolite signal intensities were found to differentiate tumor samples from nontumor tissue and they stratified glioma subtypes by IDH mutation status and by tumor grade, with several ratios showing 100% agreement with independent clinical assignments ( P < 0.0001, Mann–Whitney U test). Increased carnitine relative abundances were found across all glioma subtypes. Importantly, α-aminoadipate was significantly elevated in grade 4 glioma, which may correlate with increased tumor malignancy. Grade 3 gliomas showed markedly higher 2HG abundance than grade 4 samples. In addition, a selection of ratios showed a linear trend with varying tumor cell percentage. Overall, the multiple metabolic ratio alterations indicate a…

items.title: Pressure-induced Lifshitz and quantum phase transitions in electron-doped cuprate superconductors
items.summary_raw: We report observations of a pressure-induced Lifshitz transition coupled with a quantum phase transition in the electron-doped cuprate superconductor Pr 0.87 LaCe 0.13 CuO 4±δ , by combining high-pressure electrical resistance, Hall coefficient ( R H ), and synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD) measurements at low temperatures. Our low-temperature Hall coefficient ( R H ) measurements reveal that the R H decreases continuously and reaches zero at ~10 GPa (critical pressure of P c1 ). Upon further compression beyond P c1 , R H unexpectedly changes its sign from negative to positive, signaling a reconstruction of the Fermi surface from electron-dominated to hole-dominated topology. Concurrently, the superconducting transition temperature ( T c ) exhibits a monotonic suppression, vanishing completely at ~17.6 GPa (critical pressure of P c2 ), where the system enters a nonsuperconducting metallic state. Our low-temperature XRD measurements unequivocally demonstrate the absence of any structural phase transition across P c1 and P c2 . Therefore, the sign change in R H at P c1 is associated with a Lifshitz transition, which is never found in the compressed bulk electron- or hole-doped cuprate superconductors. Moreover, the quantum phase transition observed at P c2 contrasts sharply with known high-pressure behavior of hole-doped cuprates, uncovering a fundamental difference on how pressure tunes the ground states of electron- vs. hole-doped systems. These findings provide crucial…

items.title: Repeated marine-to-freshwater fish transitions reveal paleoenvironmental modulation of adaptive radiation
items.summary_raw: Tropical rivers in Australia and New Guinea (Sahul) provide a rare natural experiment in vertebrate evolution: Unlike other continental systems, their freshwater ichthyofaunas are composed almost entirely of marine-derived lineages rather than primary freshwater fishes. This unique biogeographic setting enables replicated tests of why some marine-to-freshwater transitions give rise to extensive adaptive radiations whereas others remain species-poor, and whether these outcomes reflect ecological opportunity or temporally structured paleoenvironmental constraints. Using a densely sampled, time-calibrated phylogenomic framework spanning 2,303 teleost species, we identified 27–34 marine-to-freshwater transitions during the Cenozoic, including a pronounced Middle Miocene peak (16–11 Ma). Although ecological opportunity in Sahul rivers enabled repeated colonization in the absence of dominant primary freshwater incumbents, younger freshwater lineages nevertheless diversify faster than older ones, contradicting the expectation that early arrivers should undergo elevated diversification when accessing vacant niche space. Although some colonizations coincide with bursts of speciation consistent with adaptive radiation, many yielded few species despite long residence times. Functional trait analyses likewise revealed no consistent relationship between colonization timing, ecological breadth, or lineage diversification rate, although expanded functional space characterizes previously…

items.title: LAT condensation gates PLCγ1 activation via bimodal LAT phosphorylation
items.summary_raw: T cells can respond to even a single molecular binding event of antigen to a TCR. A key step in the TCR signaling pathway that definitively exhibits this single-molecule response is the initiation of calcium influx by activation of PLCγ1 in the LAT protein condensate. Here, we describe detailed kinetic measurements examining how protein condensation of LAT regulates activation of PLCγ1 using a reconstituted membrane system. The results reveal that membrane recruitment of PLCγ1 is tightly controlled by the LAT phosphorylation state, with no measurable independent recruitment to PIP 2 or PIP 3 lipids via the PLCγ1 PH domains. We further observe PLCγ1 is rapidly activated by membrane-associated kinase upon recruitment, irrespective of the LAT condensation state. These studies also reveal a crosstalk mechanism in which the TEC family kinases responsible for PLCγ1 activation also phosphorylate LAT. This interaction establishes a positive feedback loop in LAT phosphorylation, mediated through LAT condensation, which drives a bimodal LAT phosphorylation response to TCR activation. Kinetic modeling reveals how this LAT phosphorylation response can cooperatively gate PLCγ1 activation from a single TCR. These results suggest the LAT condensate facilitates both signal amplification and noise suppression in PLCγ1 activation through a bimodal switch affecting LAT phosphorylation.

items.title: Profile of Shang-Ping Xie
items.summary_raw: Sea-surface temperatures are rising except in the one place models predict they should rise the most: the tropical eastern Pacific Ocean. Elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 2026, Shang-Ping Xie reconciles climate models and observations in his Inaugural Article, showing that warming is so far masked by internal variation. The climate scientist at Scripps Institution of Oceanography has examined the interactions of currents and wind throughout his career, often in service to improving prediction. Previously he showed that the Indian Ocean acts like a capacitor, driving flooding in the Yangtze River as it discharges stored warmth from El Niño.

items.title: Thermosensor OsTT3.1 enhances rice thermotolerance by degrading OsGSK2 to reduce OsHsfB2c phosphorylation and nuclear translocation
items.summary_raw: Heat stress significantly impacts rice productivity, making understanding of molecular mechanisms crucial for crop improvement. Here, we report a regulatory pathway in rice that integrates a membrane-localized E3 ubiquitin ligase (OsTT3.1), glycogen synthase kinase 2 (OsGSK2), and the heat shock factor B2c (OsHsfB2c) to modulate thermotolerance. We demonstrate that OsGSK2 directly interacts with and phosphorylates OsHsfB2c both in vitro and in vivo, a modification that promotes its nuclear translocation. Functional analyses revealed that mutations in both OsGSK2 and OsHsfB2c enhance heat tolerance, while their overexpression reduces thermotolerance. Furthermore, we identified OsTT3.1 as an OsGSK2-interacting protein that promotes OsGSK2 degradation through ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis. Double mutant analysis ( ostt3.1 / osgsk2 ) showed increased heat tolerance compared to ostt3.1 single mutants, confirming that OsTT3.1 acts upstream of OsGSK2. Transcriptomic profiling of oshsfb2c mutants under normal and heat stress conditions uncovers widespread dysregulation of genes involved in primary metabolism and stress defense, indicating that OsHsfB2c functions as a transcriptional repressor of heat-responsive pathways. Our findings establish a sophisticated regulatory cascade where OsTT3.1-mediated degradation of OsGSK2 relieves the phosphorylation of OsHsfB2c, thereby derepressing heat stress responses and enhancing thermotolerance in rice. This “brake-release” mechanism serves…

items.title: Functional similarity shapes global patterns of fish naturalization and invasion richness
items.summary_raw: Freshwater ecosystems are among the most threatened by biological invasions, but it remains unclear why some exotics are more likely to be successful (known as naturalization success) and why some communities tend to harbor more exotics than others (measured as invasion richness). Here, using trait-based analysis, we addressed the knowledge gaps based on data from 1,691 fish communities worldwide. We found a latitudinal pattern of naturalization success, showing that successful exotic species were functionally more similar to native species at high latitudes than at low latitudes. Furthermore, the latitudinal gradient of invasion success was driven by contemporary climate, with higher exotic-native functional similarity in stressful climate conditions (i.e., high latitudes), while the opposite was observed in benign climates (i.e., low latitudes). Functional similarity was further positively associated with invasion richness, suggesting that preadaptations to novel environments (i.e., high similarity) may facilitate invasion richness. Moreover, invasion richness increased with increasing basin area and human pressure, but the effect of native diversity on richness was variable. Overall, the results highlight the joint influence of ecological processes (i.e., environmental filtering and niche differentiation) and human activities on fish invasions, with the relative role of ecological processes being well-elucidated through functional similarity.

items.title: α-aminobutyric acid promotes tumor progression by polarizing macrophages through the ASNS–mTORC2 axis
items.summary_raw: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), the most abundant immune cell subset in the tumor microenvironment (TME), exhibit phenotypic plasticity and exert critical roles in tumor progression and antitumor immunity. Targeting TAM polarization has emerged as a promising strategy for cancer immunotherapy, yet the key regulators governing this process remain incompletely defined. Here, we identified α-aminobutyric acid (AABA) as a pro-tumor metabolite that drives M2-like polarization of TAMs to promote tumor progression. Mechanistically, AABA binds to asparagine synthetase (ASNS), reinforcing the mTORC2–IRF4 signaling axis to reprogram TAMs, switching macrophage metabolism from glycolysis to oxidative phosphorylation, a hallmark of pro-tumor M2-like phenotypes. Moreover, tumor-derived AABA was transported into macrophages by monocarboxylate transporters 1 and compromised the therapeutic efficacy of PD-1 checkpoint inhibition. Collectively, our findings uncover AABA as a previously unrecognized signaling metabolite to control TAM polarization, providing insights into the metabolic crosstalk within the TME and offering a potential therapeutic target to improve cancer immunotherapy outcomes.

items.title: MrtR of Mesorhizobium tianshanense reveals both activation and inhibition mechanisms of a LuxR-type quorum sensing receptor
items.summary_raw: Quorum sensing (QS) enables common gram-negative bacteria to coordinate collective behaviors through small molecule signals, yet how these signals tune receptor activity remains incompletely understood. Here, we define a mechanism by which ligand structure controls function in a LuxR-type QS receptor. Using structural and biochemical analyses, we investigate MrtR from Mesorhizobium tianshanense and show that ligand acyl-chain length governs receptor assembly and activity. We present full-length structures of MrtR bound to activating and inhibitory ligands, revealing a switch in oligomeric state. Long-chain (C14) N -acyl l -homoserine lactones (AHLs) act as agonists by promoting intra- and intersubunit interactions that lead to homodimerization and DNA binding. In contrast, shorter (C8) AHLs fail to promote these contacts, favoring a monomeric, inactive state. Ligands of intermediate length produce graded responses consistent with partial dimer stabilization. Biochemical measurements of DNA binding, thermostability, and oligomerization, together with targeted mutagenesis, support this model and establish the functional importance of key structural contacts. These findings provide a side-by-side structural comparison of a full-length LuxR-type receptor bound to both agonist and antagonist. Our results expand the known structural and mechanistic diversity of the LuxR family and suggest mechanistic similarities between structurally distinct receptors.

items.title: The Startup Raising $17 Million for Super-Thin, Wall-Mounted Batteries
items.summary_raw: Electricity is more expensive in times of peak demand — that’s simply a universal truth. But for many commercial building owners and tenants, their most energy-intensive minutes of the month can have an especially outsized impact on their electricity bill. That’s because of the “demand charge,” a fee based on a building’s single highest burst of power consumption, which can make up over 50% of a customer’s monthly bill. Likewise, shrinking those bursts would not only ease strain on the grid, but could also dramatically lower commercial users’ costs. Or at least that’s Novele’s pitch. The startup, which makes 2-inch-thick, fire-safe lithium-ion batteries that mount on the interior walls of commercial spaces such as offices, hospitals, and big box retailers, announced Wednesday that it raised an oversubscribed $17 million Series A led by impact-focused investor Boisei Labs. The funding will help the company scale its AI-powered battery system, which networks batteries placed throughout a building and uses software to predict impending spikes in power demand. Just before the peak hits, the system can automatically switch the building from grid power to battery power, helping the customer avoid those costly demand charges. “We learn how the building consumes power, but we’re also taking into account other considerations, like what day of the week it is, how the building is occupied, when it’s being used, what’s happening with the weather conditions,” Novele’s co-founder and CEO…

items.title: States want to make Big Oil pay for climate harm. Now, courts are weighing in.
items.summary_raw: Last week, another federal judge blocked New York’s so-called “climate superfund law,” the state’s attempt to make fossil fuel companies pay for climate-related damages linked to their activities. Signed in 2024, the legislation inspired other states to start drumming up their own ways to hold Big Oil financially accountable for the costs of a warming planet. The two rulings are certainly a blow to the law’s advocates. But they’re not a death knell for this approach. That’s according to seven lawmakers from Connecticut, Hawaiʻi, Rhode Island, New Jersey, and New Hampshire, who told Grist the decisions have limited relevance to their states. Most expressed continued interest in advancing their own superfund legislation. What may be more threatening to these kinds of pollution-accountability laws is Suncor v. Boulder County , a case the Supreme Court will hear beginning next week. Though a decision may not come until next spring, the outcome could nullify all state-level attempts to make fossil fuel companies pay for climate costs. “Worst case, they rule that federal law — both statutory and constitutional federal law — preempts all of these cases, throws them all out,” said Pat Parenteau, an emeritus professor at the Vermont Law School. items.title: Nebraskans couldn’t escape the heat this summer — not even at night
items.summary_raw: In Omaha, Nebraska, during the recent early September heat wave when temps hit the mid-90s Fahrenheit and lows stayed in the 70s, Pat Wilson-Johnson came to the Salvation Army’s North Corps Community Center for lunch. The location functions as a cooling center during high heat days. From growing up in Omaha, Wilson-Johnson remembers cool summer nights when she could let the breeze in through an open window. Now, she said, that just lets in the humidity. “Nine o’clock at night, it’s still 90, 91 degrees. That’s not right,” Wilson-Johnson said. Scott Harris, who works at the center, said many people will have lunch and then sit in the lobby to cool off and drink water. The location also gives out bags of ice for people to stay cool when they leave. The Siena Francis House, a nonprofit that serves people experiencing homelessness, operates another cooling center during heat advisories. While they’re typically open from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., Kristy McKern, director of case management and permanent supportive housing, said the organization has staff and protocols in case people need resources outside of these times. In Lincoln, the Lincoln-Lancaster County Health Department created an extreme heat response plan over a year ago. While the department has focused on high daytime temperatures, they are beginning to look at nighttime temperature data, a department spokesperson said. Right now, the Lincoln area has one cooling center that operates overnight. As in many other places…
