items.title: The phenotypic landscape of the model firmicute Bacillus subtilis
items.summary_raw: Firmicutes are gram-positive bacteria with important roles in human health, disease, and industry. However, more than a quarter of genes in the model firmicute Bacillus subtilis remain completely uncharacterized, including numerous phylum-specific genes. Here, we design a compact pooled CRISPRi library targeting all protein-coding genes in B. subtilis and test its growth in ~150 stress conditions. Using data from this screen as a hypothesis generator, we perform targeted experiments, revealing that the conserved essential firmicute protein YneF is part of the SRP cotranslational protein secretion pathway. We also demonstrate that ECF-transporters play a broadly conserved role in cell wall homeostasis, perform an unbiased analysis of amino acid crossfeeding, and make additional insights into bacterial competition. This work additionally provides a rich dataset to nucleate future studies of uncharacterized genes and presents a framework for performing accessible full-genome functional genomic screens in other bacteria.

items.title: Biosynthetic origin of anticancer dolastatin 15 reveals a noncanonical NRPS architecture enabling 2-keto acid activation
items.summary_raw: Elucidating the biological origins and biosynthetic pathways of marine natural products remains a major challenge, particularly for compounds derived from microbial consortia. Here, we identify the marine cyanobacterial genus Dapis as the source of the potent anticancer natural product dolastatin 15 using genome-resolved metagenomics. Reconstruction of two complete and two near-complete genomes provides genome-resolved characterization of the genus Dapis , revealing extensive biosynthetic potential. Genome mining identified the dolastatin 15 biosynthetic gene cluster. Subsequent analyses reconstructed its pathway and uncovered a noncanonical five-domain nonribosomal peptide synthetase module containing an embedded 2-keto acid–activating domain, revealing an unexpected architectural solution for incorporating 2-keto acid-derived hydroxy acid building blocks. Comparative and evolutionary analyses support a model in which this architecture may have arisen through recruitment of keto acid-activating domains and reduction of canonical adenylation domain features. We further biochemically and structurally characterize an O -methyltransferase that catalyzes formation of the characteristic methoxy pyrrolinone moiety, thereby validating a key terminal tailoring step in the proposed biosynthetic pathway. Together, these findings define the biosynthetic logic of dolastatin 15 and expand understanding of substrate activation and assembly-line diversification in nonribosomal peptide…

items.title: The PKMYT1–ALDOA axis drives chemoresistance in cholangiocarcinoma by enhancing glycolysis and MRE11 lactylation
items.summary_raw: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a highly aggressive biliary malignancy with limited responses to existing treatments. Gemcitabine plus cisplatin (GC) remains the standard first-line chemotherapy for advanced disease, but its clinical efficacy is suboptimal, and drug resistance frequently emerges in patients. Through high-throughput synergistic drug screening, we identified PKMYT1 as a key synthetic lethal target regulating the chemosensitivity of cholangiocarcinoma cells. Functional validation confirmed that the PKMYT1 small-molecule inhibitor RP6306 exerts robust synthetic lethal effects when used in combination with gemcitabine or cisplatin. Data from colony formation assays and a series of cellular functional experiments showed that genetic or pharmacological inhibition of PKMYT1 substantially compromises DNA damage repair (DDR) and induces massive DNA double-strand breaks. Further mechanistic investigations revealed that PKMYT1 binds to Aldolase A (encoded by the ALDOA gene) and enhances its enzymatic activity, thereby upregulating CCA glycolysis levels and inducing lactate accumulation, which ultimately elevates the lactylation level of MRE11, accelerates DDR and consequently drives chemoresistance in CCA. Both cell-derived and patient-derived xenograft models verified that combined treatment with RP6306 and GC markedly inhibits tumor growth in vivo. Taken together, this work reveals that the PKMYT1-ALDOA-mediated protein lactylation pathway acts as a critical regulator of…

items.title: Mechanisms of substrate recognition and catalysis in a mammalian phosphatidylserine synthase 2
items.summary_raw: Mammalian phosphatidylserine synthase-1 and -2, PSS1 and PSS2, synthesize phosphatidylserine (PS) by replacing the headgroup of either phosphatidylcholine or phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) with a serine. We determined structures of PSS2 from Equus caballus in complex with either a PE or a serine substrate to resolutions of 2.8 to 3.2 Å. The structures define substrate binding sites and reveal that the phosphate group of the PE is coordinated by two Ca 2+ . In addition, we found that PSS2 has significant phospholipase D (PLD) activity in the absence of serine and that Ca 2+ is required for the PLD activity. These findings enrich and refine our knowledge in the mechanisms of substrate recognition and catalysis in mammalian PSS.

items.title: Distribution and voltage dependence of ion channels shape single-neuron computations
items.summary_raw: Voltage-gated ion channels do not distribute evenly in the plasma membrane of a neuron; they localize to distinct domains where they govern the excitability of the cell and the computations it performs. Informed by electron microscopic reconstructions, models of morphologically realistic neurons offer the opportunity to study these computations, but they lack constraints on the subcellular localizations and functional properties of voltage-gated channels. Here, we address this problem in Drosophila melanogaster by developing tools to tag and visualize endogenous ion channels in genetically designated populations of cells and in single neurons. Focusing on a suite of highly expressed ion channels in visual motion-sensitive neurons, we report their subcellular localizations and their steady-state activation and inactivation curves. Integrating these structural and functional data into a biophysically constrained model reproduces the directional tuning of motion-sensitive T5 neurons and reveals the function of voltage-gated sodium channels in nonspiking neurons.

items.title: Chain organization of dimple-ended magnetite magnetosomes supports field-dependent cell linking in unicellular magnetotactic bacteria
items.summary_raw: Magnetotactic bacteria (MTB) are generally thought to navigate as individual cells by using intracellular magnetosome chains that provide a stable magnetic moment for orientation along magnetic field lines. Whether nonclassical magnetosome geometries and particle-scale magnetic states can support robust chain-level magnetic function, and potentially mediate interactions between cells, remains unresolved. Here, to we report a unicellular magnetotactic bacterium, strain WYHV-1, that biomineralizes comparatively large prismatic magnetite magnetosomes with distinctive dimples at both crystal ends and organizes them into a single tightly packed intracellular chain. Off-axis electron holography reveals that individual dimple-ended particles commonly exhibit single-vortex behavior rather than a canonical uniformly magnetized single-domain (SD) state. Micromagnetic simulations indicate a size-dependent transition from SD to single-vortex behavior in dimple-ended particles and that tight intrachain coupling suppresses particle-scale nonuniformity, producing a predominantly SD-like magnetization within the chain and a strong chain-parallel remanent moment. Further simulations indicate that chain-generated stray fields concentrated at chain ends can generate intercellular magnetic attraction strong enough to promote head-to-tail linking between neighboring cells over subcellular distances. These results provide a physical explanation for field-dependent multicell-like assemblies…

items.title: Desulfinylation of the deubiquitinase USP7 by SRXN1 attenuates oxidative acute liver injury
items.summary_raw: Protein S -sulfinylation is a reversible oxidative cysteine modification, but its contribution to acute liver injury such as those induced by acetaminophen (APAP) overdose has not been reported. Sulfiredoxin-1 (SRXN1) is the only oxidoreductase known to reduce the sulfinylated proteins, yet the substrates and mechanisms through which it protects against acute liver injury are unclear. Here, we show that hepatic protein S -sulfinylation was markedly upregulated in APAP-overdose patients and mice. Hepatocyte-specific knockout or pharmacological inhibition of Srxn1 sensitized mice to APAP-induced acute liver injury. In contrast, overexpression of SRXN1, but not its oxidoreductase-dead C99S mutant, protected mice from APAP-induced liver injury. Mechanistically, we identified the deubiquitinase ubiquitin-specific protease 7 (USP7) as an SRXN1 substrate required for hepatoprotection. USP7 inhibition worsened APAP-induced liver injury, whereas its overexpression alleviated injury by stabilizing its deubiquitinase substrate heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1). Loss of SRXN1 enhanced S -sulfinylation of USP7 at Cys315, promoting its ubiquitination and degradation. SRXN1 expression correlated with USP7 levels in human liver samples. Delayed lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery of SRXN1 messenger RNA (mRNA) mitigated established APAP-induced liver injury beyond the therapeutic window of N -acetylcysteine. These findings define an SRXN1-USP7-HO-1 axis as a promising therapeutic target for oxidative…

items.title: Reproducible cortical links between functional hierarchy, structure, and metabolism
items.summary_raw: Large-scale functional connectivity gradients provide a compact description of cortical organization, capturing hierarchical transitions from unimodal sensory systems to transmodal association cortex. Although these gradients have become a central framework for studying macroscale brain organization, it remains unclear whether they systematically map onto regional cortical biology. Here we show that functional gradient position robustly predicts cortical thickness and regional glucose metabolism, measured with MRI and FDG-PET respectively. Modeling parcelwise cortical thickness and glucose metabolism as linear combinations of signed and amplitude components along functional gradients explained substantial variance in both measures across individuals, with signed gradient terms improving prediction in every subject. These relationships generalized across scanning sessions and independent cohorts and remained significant under spatial permutation testing. Gradient-based models outperformed classical graph-theoretic connectivity metrics, whereas nonlinear extensions did not improve performance. Cortical myelin was selectively associated with the signed component of the principal gradient, without an amplitude effect, and this pattern replicated across developmental, adult, and aging cohorts, supporting a microstructural basis for gradient-cortical thickness coupling. In contrast, gradient associations with glucose metabolism remained largely intact after controlling for…

items.title: Loss of cerebral autoregulation drives abnormal perfusion patterns after stroke
items.summary_raw: Maintaining a stable cerebral blood flow (CBF) despite variations in blood pressure is crucial for normal brain function. This process, called cerebral autoregulation, is often impaired in pathologies such as ischemic stroke, underlining its clinical importance. However, how local vascular responses interact across complex cerebrovascular networks to stabilize perfusion remains poorly understood. Here, we present an in silico model of static autoregulation that can be applied to realistic microvascular networks, providing vessel-specific insights into vasoreactivity and perfusion dynamics. Our simulations revealed a hierarchical organization of autoregulatory responses, in which pial surface arteries act as key regulators that buffer pressure changes across large vascular territories. Arterial density emerged as a decisive determinant of network-specific autoregulatory capacity, highlighting the importance of vascular topology for maintaining stable perfusion. During poststroke reperfusion, alterations in vasoreactivity, rather than collateral extent alone, emerged as the main contributor to pathogenic hyperperfusion. Simulations of chronic autoregulatory dysfunction showed that progressive loss of vascular reactivity can produce substantial downstream disturbances in capillary perfusion and alter the autoregulation curve. Overall, our framework reveals how interactions between vascular topology and vessel-specific regulatory mechanisms shape CBF regulation across scales…

items.title: TCR–mTORC1 signaling promotes epigenetic stabilization of Foxp3 expression in regulatory T cells via TET protein translation
items.summary_raw: Regulatory T (Treg) cell differentiation and function rely on stable expression of the master transcription factor Foxp3. While Foxp3 expression is epigenetically stabilized through DNA demethylation of a Foxp3 enhancer (the Treg-specific demethylated region, TSDR), the mechanisms underlying this process remain unclear. Here, we show that strong and sustained T cell receptor (TCR) signaling promotes TSDR demethylation, stabilizes Foxp3 expression, and confers suppressive activity in in vitro–induced Treg (iTreg) cells through activation of mTORC1. Mechanistically, TCR–mTORC1 signaling promotes TSDR demethylation by enhancing translation of TET2, and likely TET3, enzymes that mediate DNA demethylation. Rescue of impaired TSDR demethylation under mTORC1 inhibition by the TET2 catalytic domain, together with dose-dependent impairment following heterozygous deficiency of TET2 and/or TET3, supports a causal link between TET protein abundance and TSDR demethylation. In vivo, mTORC1 inactivation increases the frequency of cells harboring a methylated TSDR among peripheral Foxp3 + T cells, but not among developing Foxp3 + thymocytes, supporting in vivo relevance of mTORC1-dependent epigenetic remodeling. Thus, TCR–mTORC1 signaling promotes epigenetic stabilization of Foxp3 expression through translational control of TET proteins, revealing an unrecognized role for mTORC1 in iTreg cell differentiation.

items.title: Deletions in variable region 1 of the HIV envelope accelerate V3-glycan bNAb induction in SHIV-infected rhesus macaques
items.summary_raw: Elicitation of broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs) is a major goal of HIV-1 vaccine research. V3-glycan bNAbs were previously identified in a person living with HIV-1, CH848, and in two of six rhesus macaques (RMs) infected with a simian-HIV (SHIV) expressing the CH848 transmitted/founder envelope (Env) glycoprotein. In all cases, neutralization breadth developed after years of infection and only after the variable region 1 (V1) of Env had shortened in response to neutralizing antibodies. These observations suggested that V3-glycan bNAb elicitation might be accelerated if RMs were infected with SHIVs bearing CH848 Envs with truncated V1 loops. To test this hypothesis, we analyzed NAb responses in 10 RMs infected with SHIV.CH848 variants containing V1 deletions that mimicked those observed in natural infection. In three RMs, potent V3-glycan bNAbs developed within 1 y of infection, nearly three times faster than in wildtype CH848 infection. Longitudinal sequencing of B cell immunoglobulin genes revealed a single bNAb lineage in each RM that was primed as early as 8 to 12 wk postinfection and that largely recapitulated plasma breadth. A meta-analysis of the frequency of V3-glycan bNAb induction in RMs infected by SHIVs expressing CH848-derived Envs vs. 15 other primary HIV-1 Envs demonstrated a substantial enhancement in the CH848 group (5 of 16 vs. 2 of 109; P = 0.0003). We conclude that CH848 Envs have a propensity for inducing V3-glycan bNAbs and that truncations in…

items.title: Loss of CsrA in Acinetobacter baumannii leads to lethal dysregulation of alanine metabolism
items.summary_raw: Posttranscriptional regulation is a key mechanism by which bacteria coordinate gene expression in response to changing environments. In the human pathogen Acinetobacter baumannii , the importance of posttranscriptional gene expression control is exemplified by CsrA, a highly conserved posttranscriptional regulator that is essential for viability in multiple settings, ranging from growth in rich laboratory media to infection-relevant conditions like human serum. However, csrA is dispensable for growth in chemically defined media with a single carbon source. We leveraged this condition-specific essentiality to identify suppressor mutations that regained the ability to grow in rich media. These analyses identified Lrp, a transcription factor that regulates hundreds of genes in A. baumannii. Among the Lrp regulon, we identified a four gene locus involved with uptake and utilization of D-alanine. We determined that two transcripts encoded by this locus, dadA and cycA2 , are repressed by CsrA. The absence of csrA leads to overexpression of both dadA and cycA2 , which is toxic, even in wild type A. baumannii . In the csrA mutant, this dysregulation contributes to impaired cell envelope integrity and increased sensitivity to several clinically relevant cell-wall targeting antibiotics, including carbapenems. Collectively, our data indicate that Lrp and CsrA coordinately balance expression of D-alanine utilization genes in A. baumannii , at the transcriptional and posttranscriptional…

items.title: SRSF3 plays a key role in liver cancer sex disparity by facilitating hepatocyte expression of ERα and FOXA
items.summary_raw: SRSF3 (SRp20) is an essential RNA splicing factor. By conditional knockout (KO) of Srsf3, we found Srsf3 at its physiological level plays a tumor-suppressive role in mouse liver carcinogenesis. Srsf3 KO in hepatocytes disrupted sex disparity in the development of DEN-induced liver cancer and resulted in high incidence of liver cancer in both male and female mice. In contrast, Srsf3 is oncogenic in the mouse mammary glands and Srsf3 KO significantly delayed the development of Erbb2 breast cancer. Srsf3 KO significantly increased the expression of transcription factors Sox4, E2f1, and Myc, calcium channel factor Trpv4, and zinc-binding Trim6 in liver cancer, but did not in Erbb2 breast cancer. Srsf3 KO enhanced the expression of glucose transmembrane transporter Mfsd4a and translation initiator Eif4a2 in DEN-induced liver cancer but reduced Mfsd4a and Eif4a2 expression in breast cancer. More importantly, Srsf3 KO reduced the expression of hepatocyte ERα and transcription factor Foxa family genes essential for sexual dimorphism in liver cancer and their downstream targets leukemia inhibitory factor receptor Lifr and epidermal growth factor receptor Egfr, but increased the expression of Myc. We further evidenced that SRSF3 binds to FOXA1 promoter and is responsible for FOXA1 promoter activity and FOXA1 expression in liver cancer cells. Together, our data highlight a functional paradigm of SRSF3 at its physiological level in tissue context-dependent gene regulation and in…

items.title: Functional brain networks underlying approach–avoidance conflict processing in humans and rats
items.summary_raw: Our ability to arbitrate between competing approach and avoidance motivations is thought to be an emergent property, arising from the coordinated activity of functional brain networks. Parallel lines of investigation in human and rodent research have identified candidate hub regions supporting approach–avoidance conflict (AAC) behavior, namely the anterior (ventral) hippocampus and prefrontal cortex; yet, a cross-species elucidation of the network dynamics supporting learned conflict processing has yet to be demonstrated. Here, we sought to bridge this translational gap by conducting a functional network analysis in humans and rats from brain-wide neural activity generated by learned motivational conflict. We found that the anterior hippocampus in humans and ventral hippocampus in rats occupied highly central hub-like positions in the network and were highly integrated with extrinsic functional communities. The insula, particularly the posterior insula in rats, was also identified as a putative cross-species hub. Finally, we identified shifts in network topology based on individual differences and sex in conflict preference. Our findings provide evidence for conserved network dynamics, particularly at the regional scale, supporting AAC processing in humans and rats.

items.title: Healing cascades and infections in wounds monitored using a wearable sensor of gaseous flux
items.summary_raw: Capabilities for quantitative monitoring of chronic wounds remain an unmet clinical need, as existing diagnostic approaches rely on semiquantitative evaluation of symptoms that lack sensitivity especially during early stages of infection. Here, we present a scheme for tracking wound physiology that leverages a miniature, wireless skin-interfaced device for noncontact, transient measurements of the flux of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and water vapor from the wound microenvironment. Unlike emerging smart bandage platforms that rely on physical contact with the fragile wound bed to interrogate liquid-phase biomarkers, this strategy uses an engineered microclimate and suspended suite of sensors to measure the diffusive transport of wound-derived gases across the wound surface but separated from it. The result enables quantitative evaluation of metabolic activity and healing progression without perturbing the healing tissues. In biofilm growth models of Staphylococcus aureus , measurements demonstrate that trends in VOC flux correlate strongly with bacterial growth kinetics and precede any visible biofilm formation. Longitudinal monitoring of infected and noninfected wounds on diabetic mice shows that concurrent measurements of water vapor and VOC flux provide complementary physiological insights, capturing both the trajectory of barrier restoration and the dynamics of bacterial burden. The findings establish this noncontact sensing scheme as a distinct and clinically…

items.title: The Ca 2+ channel CYCLIC NUCLEOTIDE GATED CHANNEL13 regulates vasculature-mediated systemic Ca 2+ and jasmonate signaling on herbivory
items.summary_raw: Insect herbivory triggers rapid local and systemic signaling in plants, including membrane depolarization, cytosolic Ca 2+ elevation, and activation of jasmonate-mediated defense pathways. These early events are shaped by calcium-permeable ion channels and regulatory components that generate stimulus-specific Ca 2+ signatures. The glutamate receptor-like channel-centric model of long-distance Ca 2+ signaling is insufficient to explain the robustness of systemic responses to diverse damage and herbivore cues, indicating the involvement of additional Ca 2+ channels. Here, we identify CYCLIC NUCLEOTIDE GATED CHANNEL13 (CNGC13) as a plasma membrane–localized, vasculature-expressed Ca 2+ channel that is essential for systemic jasmonate signaling and defense against lepidopteran insect pest, Spodoptera litura in Arabidopsis thaliana . CNGC13 is rapidly induced by wounding and herbivory and is required for efficient propagation of Ca 2+ signals from wounded to distal leaves. Loss of CNGC13 compromises the thioglucosidase (Ricca factor)-dependent breakdown of aliphatic glucosinolates into aglucones/isothiocyanates within the vascular tissue, which are essential for wound-induced systemic Ca 2+ wave propagation. Consequently, cngc13 mutants display reduced wound induced jasmonate accumulation in systemic leaves, reduced glucosinolate levels and enhanced herbivore susceptibility. CNGC13 is also required for At Pep-induced Ca 2+ elevation and reactive oxygen species signaling and…

items.title: Phosphoproteomic dysregulation promotes tumor proliferation in Cushing’s disease
items.summary_raw: Pituitary adenomas constitute up to 20% of primary brain tumors, yet somatic mutations are only found in 15% of pituitary adenomas. Epigenomic dysregulation has been proposed as a tumorigenic mechanism in pituitary adenomas causing Cushing’s disease (CD). We created paired datasets of human CD adenomas and en-route margin adult human pituitary glands, and assayed their chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, transcriptomic, proteomic, and phospho-proteomic landscapes. In CD adenomas, we found epigenetic reactivation of a neurodevelopmental phosphoprotein program typically lost in the postnatal pituitary gland. CD cells overexpressed PPP1R17 , an endogenous inhibitor of the protein phosphatase PP2A. Mechanistically, PPP1R17 overexpression in normal murine pituitary cells recapitulated the adenoma phenotype, and the resulting hyperproliferation was reversed in a PP2A-dependent manner by fingolimod, an FDA-approved small molecule, both in vitro and in vivo. Our findings highlight kinase-phosphatase imbalance as a targetable mechanism in CD.

items.title: Associative synaptic plasticity creates dynamic persistent activity
items.summary_raw: In biological neural circuits, the dynamics of neurons and synapses are tightly coupled. We study the consequences of this coupling and show that it enables a form of working memory. In recurrent neural network models with ongoing Hebbian plasticity, we find that following oscillatory stimulation, neurons continue to oscillate long after the input is removed. This creates a dynamic form of memory that has no explicit storage or retrieval phases and that requires no prior knowledge of the input. We trace the mechanism of these “persistent oscillations” to an interaction between neurons and synapses that creates complex outlier eigenvalues of the connectivity matrix. This is shown both in simulation and analytically. We leverage this mechanistic understanding to generate persistent oscillations with prespecified dynamics, creating a dynamic analog of a classical Hopfield network. Our work demonstrates that coupling neuronal and synaptic dynamics enables novel forms of computation.

items.title: PKD2-like proteins target Chlamydomonas PKD2 to distinct subciliary regions
items.summary_raw: Many motile and sensory functions of cilia and flagella depend on the precise localization of transmembrane proteins within the ciliary membrane. Rather than being uniformly distributed, these proteins are often targeted to specific subciliary regions along the length or circumference of cilia. Here, we use genome editing and in vivo imaging to dissect the spatial organization of the channel protein PKD2 in Chlamydomonas cilia. MST3, a PKD2-like protein with five transmembrane helices (5TMH), is localized exclusively to the distal cilium, where it is essential for the localization of PKD2 and the formation of the hair-like mastigonemes. MST3, however, is dispensable for PKD2 assembly in the proximal cilium. In contrast, the PKD2-like 5TMH protein Proximal PKD2 Interactor (PPI) resides in the proximal cilium, where it is required for PKD2 assembly; ppi mutants retain distal PKD2 and mastigonemes. In mst3 ppi double knockouts, both proximal and distal PKD2 are absent, revealing that MST3 and PPI organize PKD2 into distal and proximal regions. Further, PKD2 colocalizes and comigrates with PKD2-like protein 1 (PLP1), another 5TMH protein, in cilia, indicating that they are present together in a complex. While plp1 mutants swim largely normally, mst3 and, to a lesser degree, ppi mutants swim with reduced velocity, indicating a functional specialization of the different ciliary PKD2 complexes. Thus, Chlamydomonas PKD2 associates with one of several 5TMH proteins to form spatially…

items.title: Twisted Rényi negativity as a reliable proxy for mixed-state entanglement in fermionic systems
items.summary_raw: Characterizing mixed-state entanglement in fermionic quantum matter represents a fundamental challenge at the intersection of condensed matter physics and quantum information. Unlike pure states, mixed states lack a universally accepted and easily computable entanglement measure, a difficulty compounded in fermionic systems by the ambiguity of the partial transpose operation. Here, motivated by the Hermiticity of the partially transposed density matrix and the analytic continuation of the Rényi negativity to logarithmic negativity, we address this puzzle by demonstrating the “twisted” Rényi negativity as a physically consistent proxy for mixed-state entanglement in the Hubbard and spinless t - V models. Through large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations of these paradigmatic correlated systems, we show that this indicator captures essential physical expectations—including the area law and monotonic thermal suppression—while excluding anomalous behavior present in alternative definitions. Our findings not only provide a robust theoretical framework for quantifying entanglement in strongly correlated electronic systems but also offer a practical tool for experimental detection in rapidly developing platforms, including ultracold atomic gases and programmable quantum simulators.

items.title: Slc35a1-mediated endothelial sialylation controls the fate and integrity of the intestinal microvascular network in adult mice
items.summary_raw: Vascular endothelial cells express abundant sialylated glycans, but their function remains unclear. To determine the role of endothelial overall sialylation, which is controlled by Slc35a1 , in adult mice. We generated mice with inducible deletion of Slc35a1 in endothelial cells (iEHC Slc35a1 –/– ) using tamoxifen-inducible Cdh5Cre ERT2 . Induced deletion of Slc35a1 in adulthood caused progressive weight loss, anemia, and spontaneous intestinal bleeding. Adult intestinal villus capillaries exhibited disorganized networks, loss of vascular integrity, and bleeding. Multiplexed Error-Robust Fluorescence in Situ Hybridization spatial transcriptomic analysis revealed downregulation of endothelial genes essential for angiogenesis and endothelial specialization, including Vegfr2 , Cdh5 , and Plvap . Immunostaining confirmed loss of VEGFR2, disorganized VE-cadherin junctions, and impaired PLVAP-dependent capillary fenestration. Endothelial Slc35a1 deletion also reduced endothelial von Willebrand factor expression and plasma multimerization, indicating impaired hemostatic function. Our results reveal new roles for Slc35a1 -dependent endothelial sialylation in maintaining the fate and integrity of the intestinal microvascular network in adult mice.

items.title: Which AI Models Use the Most Energy?
items.summary_raw: The rise of artificial intelligence is driving an historic surge in electricity demand that’s boosting fossil fuel use and threatening climate progress. All this electricity doesn’t power AI in some generalized, always-on way, though. Data centers’ energy consumption is a function of the millions of individual queries users submit to AI programs such as Claude and ChatGPT. When it comes to how efficiently models process those queries and generate responses, AI models are not interchangeable. Some are more like gas guzzlers, others more like Priuses. When a user engages an AI chatbot or AI agent, however, there’s essentially no way for them to know which kind of vehicle they are stepping into. They may know which company built it, and even the precise model name and number, but no AI company has published information about how much energy one model uses compared to another. In the absence of corporate disclosure from the big three proprietary AI developers — Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google — researchers with the Sustainable AI Group, a research and advisory company, developed a backdoor method to estimate and compare the amount of energy these developers’ models consume. They published their findings on Tuesday in an interactive dashboard that ranks AI programs by energy intensity. “We think this is an important next step to get some science-based information out there to help folks start making better decisions,” Boris Gamazaychikov, the CEO of the Sustainable AI Group, told…

Since then, the administration has frozen or withdrawn billions of dollars in federal funding from top schools and launched investigations into them, using its leverage to influence admissions, hiring, and DEI policies. The consequences have been stark: According to the Academic Freedom Index, institutional autonomy in the United States dropped sharply last year, placing it on a steeper descent than those seen in Hungary, Turkey, and India. A new study argues that this attack didn’t come out of nowhere. In the paper recently published in the journal Energy Research & Social Science, researchers show how corporate interests, including oil companies, have sought to influence universities for at least half a century, using big donations to shape research agendas. items.title: Does populist anti-climate rhetoric drive public opposition to climate policy? Testing socio-cultural and economic frames
items.summary_raw: Right-wing populist (RWP) parties increasingly oppose climate policies, framing them as economically costly or imposed by an out-of-touch elite. Yet, little is known about the impact of such rhetoric on individuals or whether counter-frames can mitigate its effects. Using a pre-registered, UK-based survey experiment, we test whether exposure to either of these anti-climate frames influences attitudes and behaviour towards the UK’s ‘net-zero’ goal. We also test whether a counter-frame could alleviate these effects. We find both negative frames reduce support for net zero, with the economic frame showing stronger, more robust effects than the socio-cultural frame, and the counter-frame was ineffective. Still, even among those exposed to the negative economic frame, a majority supported the net zero goal (58%) and related policies (55%). Nonetheless, this study highlights the challenge to climate policy posed by RWP parties and suggests mere promises of compensatory benefits may be insufficient to build popular support.

items.title: Ethical agency and worker precarity amid polycrisis: a protest narrative analysis
items.summary_raw: Abstract: This study explores the ethical dimensions of worker precarity and protest agency in the context of ongoing polycrisis conditions in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. Drawing upon publicly available protest videos from various occupational groups-such as healthcare, education, and public sector employees-the study employs a thematic analysis to identify recurring patterns of ethical discourse, institutional critique, and collective resistance. A total of six protest cases were analyzed. The findings reveal six overarching ethical themes: precarity and vulnerability, moral agency and resistance, institutional betrayal, collective dignity and solidarity, justice-oriented appeals, and emotional exhaustion. These themes reflect how workers’ lived experiences are morally constructed and publicly articulated as demands for justice, recognition, and accountability. Radar diagrams further quantify the relative intensity of each theme across protest categories. The results suggest that workers do not merely react to material deprivation but frame their struggles through ethical language and civic engagement, thereby demonstrating moral resilience amid systemic neglect. This study contributes to the literature on business ethics, worker agency, and crisis governance by highlighting how ethical imagination and protest narratives are mobilized from the margins in response to institutional failures. It also raises implications for organizational ethics, public accountability, and the…

items.title: Students’ conceptions of climate change impacts on natural ecosystems
items.summary_raw: Climate change, driven by human activity, is a major societal issue with significant biological consequences. The purpose of this study is to investigate students’ understanding of the biological impacts of climate change on natural ecosystems. We applied a qualitative approach using open-ended questions in two ecological contexts: a temperate forest and high Arctic ecosystems. Responses from high school and undergraduate students were analysed using qualitative content analysis, focusing on different levels of biological organisation. Our findings indicate that students predominantly focus on observable effects at the individual level, while interactions between species and long-term, systemic consequences are mentioned less frequently. References to species-level impacts are largely limited to extinction, with little consideration of broader evolutionary processes. These results suggest that students’ understanding of climate change impacts remains focused on immediate and visible effects, with less awareness of complex ecological and evolutionary dynamics. The implications for teaching and learning are that instruction should more explicitly support students in connecting individual-level effects to broader ecological interactions and long-term biological processes.

items.title: Who accepts parking pricing? trust and legitimacy in a contentious policy change
items.source_name: Transportation Research Part A Policy and Practice
items.summary_raw: This paper examines public responses to the introduction of paid visitor parking as a contentious local policy change in a tourism-dependent region. While parking pricing is widely recognised as an effective tool for managing demand and generating revenue, less is known about how such policies are interpreted and legitimised by affected communities. Using the Blue Mountains in New South Wales as a case study, the study treats the introduction of paid parking as a natural (albeit deliberate policy change) experiment in user-pays reform under conditions of infrastructure funding pressure and climate-related disruption. A mixed-methods approach is employed, combining survey data, factor analysis, clustering, and qualitative thematic analysis to identify patterns in attitudes and interpretation. The findings show that acceptance is not primarily driven by demographic characteristics or behavioural exposure, but by institutional trust, beliefs about collective responsibility, and perceptions of governance quality. Three distinct attitudinal segments are identified, reflecting differing configurations of support, trust, and normative beliefs. Despite the scheme’s demonstrated effectiveness as a revenue-generating instrument capable of supporting substantial infrastructure investment, public acceptance remains contested. The policy is frequently interpreted through a “revenue raising” frame, particularly where trust is limited. The paper argues that parking pricing operates not…

items.title: When climate policy resonates: the interplay of framing, party preference, and political trust in shaping policy acceptance
items.summary_raw: Abstract This article examines whether the effectiveness of three justification framings for a road traffic emission trading system (ETS) in increasing public acceptance depends on political party preference and levels of political trust. The framings emphasized increased energy independence, economic resilience, and efficient climate mitigation. Data were collected via an online survey experiment in Finland, March 2024 ( n = 1,485). Although the justification effects were generally limited, the energy independence framing increased policy acceptance among supporters of the populist radical right Finns Party. Moreover, justification effects were minimal among individuals with high political trust but tended to trigger backlash among those with low trust. Our findings contribute to the literature on climate policy communication by showing that framing effects on policy acceptance depend not only on political preferences but also on political trust.

items.title: The contribution of World Bank financing to Türkiye’s green transition: An examination of renewable energy projects in Türkiye
items.summary_raw: Although the role of multilateral development banks in renewable energy financing has attracted increasing attention in the literature, there is limited evidence regarding the project-level characteristics of World Bank-financed renewable energy investments in Türkiye. This gap is particularly important given Türkiye’s growing commitment to sustainable development and green transition objectives. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to examine the renewable energy projects financed by the World Bank in Türkiye through a qualitative document analysis approach. Between 2000 and 2024, a total of 14 renewable energy projects were identified, one of which was canceled at the draft stage. In addition, three projects were designed as additional financing for previously approved projects. The projects evaluated in this study reached a total cost of approximately USD 6 billion, of which nearly USD 5 billion was financed by the World Bank. This demonstrates that international development finance constitutes a highly important resource for Türkiye’s transition to renewable energy. The financing provided by the World Bank has not only been limited to alternative energy production but has also encouraged the participation of both the private sector and public institutions in green energy investments. Overall, the World Bank’s financing policies toward renewable energy projects in Türkiye support the country’s sustainable development goals. These financial supports play a critical role…

items.title: Fueled by sunlight, clouded by concern: Risk perceptions and risk-risk tradeoffs regarding solar fuels from artificial photosynthesis in Germany
items.summary_raw: Mitigating climate change requires societal transformation, including decarbonization innovations, as CO 2 emissions remain the primary driver of global warming. One emerging solution is solar fuels, produced through artificial photosynthesis by integrating green hydrogen, carbon capture and utilization, and engineered microorganisms. While solar fuels offer a pathway for reusing CO 2 and reducing fossil resource dependency, they also generate new risks, uncertainties, and complex risk-risk tradeoffs. Traditional risk assessments rely on expert judgments of probability and impact, overlooking public risk perceptions shaped by personal values and experience. Yet these lay perceptions are critical for public acceptance of sustainable technologies: neglecting them risks public resistance, legitimacy deficits, and implementation failure. This study is the first to systematically map and quantify lay risk perceptions of solar fuels. We used mental model interviews ( N = 24) to map and categorize laypeople's perceived risks associated with (1) the solar fuel production process and (2) the resulting fuel product. Perceived risks were categorized using established typologies of risk types and risk-risk tradeoffs. A confirmatory survey ( N = 292) quantified perceived salience of these risks. Results indicated that production spanned all categories (natural, technological, biological, economic, demographic, political, and medical risks), while product risks excluded natural ones…

items.title: Multi-objective hybrid renewable energy planning for port decarbonisation: marine-resource complementarity, storage choice and abatement economics
items.summary_raw: A small Mediterranean port can cut its electricity-related greenhouse-gas emissions by four fifths while paying less per kilowatt-hour than its retail tariff, provided its renewable supply is designed as an integrated portfolio. The study asks which local resources belong in that portfolio, which storage should support it and whether a carbon price changes the answer. A grid-connected photovoltaic, wind, wave and tidal system with battery or hydrogen storage is sized for a Trans-European Transport Network port from hourly series: 28 configurations by a seeded, replicated genetic algorithm, then the cost against lifecycle-emissions frontier by non-dominated sorting. The cost-optimal design (360 kW photovoltaic, 112 kW wind, 30 wave converter units, 1512 kWh of battery storage) supplies electricity at EUR 0.1996/kWh against a EUR 0.36/kWh tariff and cuts annual emissions from 678.7 to 124.7 t CO 2 -eq (81.6%). Twenty of the 22 co-located configurations abate carbon while reducing cost, at EUR -396 to -5 per tonne, so the investment needs no carbon price; deepening decarbonisation along the frontier costs 493 EUR/t, and within the eight-hour frontier no step between neighbouring designs exceeds the search’s single-run variability; only the move to sixteen hours of autonomy does. Wave energy earns its place by generating in all 8760 hours and supplying 40.7% of its energy at night; the local tidal current never reaches the 1.25 m/s cut-in. Batteries beat hydrogen and hybrid…

items.title: Emotional divergence in urban climate discourse: spatial patterns and semantic decoding across global cities
items.summary_raw: Climate discourse on social media is increasingly influential in shaping public interpretations of climate risks and motivating urban climate action, yet its underlying emotional and semantic architectures remain insufficiently understood. Here, we analyze 104,274 climate-related tweets (Dec 2021-Mar 2023), of which 56,556 are geolocated, using hybrid sentiment classification, latent topic modeling, and spatial clustering to examine spatiotemporal dynamics and urban-scale variation in affective expression across 1129 cities in 78 countries. We find that climate sentiment is highly event-responsive yet structurally constrained, with emotional extremity rarely exceeding 15% even during major climate shocks. Spatially, cities in the Global North show more systematically negative or ambivalent sentiment, whereas cities in the Global South tend toward positive or activist-oriented optimism. Twelve discursive themes are identified. Semantic-affective decoupling further shows that adaptation- and development-related themes correlate with positive sentiment, while denial- or institutional-critique narratives are predominantly negative. Further, spatial clustering reveals that major metropolitan areas converge into shared emotional-discursive regimes regardless of geographic location, whereas smaller and peripheral cities diverge markedly in their group affective tone. Understanding the interplay among emotion, meaning, and urban context can inform climate narratives and support the…

items.title: Resistance as climate change mitigation: Contested emissions from Japan's anti-coal movement
items.summary_raw: Grassroots resistance increasingly shapes sustainability transformations, yet its implications for climate change mitigation remain difficult to identify and quantify. This paper introduces the concept of ‘contested emissions’ to make visible the climate significance of such struggles and develops an operational framework for estimating the emissions associated with carbon-intensive projects subject to social contestation. Contested emissions refer to the projected greenhouse gas emissions from projects opposed by local communities, activists, or social movements, including struggles that are not primarily framed around climate change. We distinguish four types of contested emissions: those associated with project cancellations, delays in operation, shortened operational lifespans, and constraints on fossil-fuel markets. We apply the framework to coal-related conflicts in Japan using data from the Environmental Justice Atlas, Global Energy Monitor, and local environmental organisations. We estimate that the opposition has been associated with the cancellation of projects representing approximately 49 million tonnes (Mt) of annual CO₂ emissions, while projects representing a further 2.4 Mt. have been delayed and 2.4 Mt. are associated with reduced operational lifespans. In addition, projects representing approximately 258 Mt. of annual CO2 emissions have been subject to continuing contestation associated with market constraints. Taken together, these resistances are…

items.title: Climate Knowledge in Large Language Models
items.source_name: Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems
items.summary_raw: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed for climate-related applications, where understanding internal climatological knowledge is important for assessing their reliability. Despite growing adoption, the capacity of LLMs to recall climate normals from parametric knowledge (information stored in the model's weights, without external retrieval) remains largely uncharacterized. We investigate this capacity focusing on a prototypical query: mean July 2-m air temperature 1991-2020 at specified locations. We construct a global grid of queries at 1° resolution land points, providing coordinates and location descriptors, and validate responses against ERA5 reanalysis. We further extend the evaluation to the twelve monthly normals for four of our best-performing LLMs on a subset of the grid. Results show that LLMs reproduce broad geographic regularities in climatological temperature fields, capturing latitudinal and topographic patterns, with July root-mean-square errors of 3-6 °C and biases of ±1 °C; errors are comparable across the annual cycle. However, spatially coherent errors remain: performance degrades sharply above 1500 m, where RMSE reaches 5-13 °C compared to 2-4 °C at lower elevations. Including geographic context (country, city, region) reduces errors by 27% on average. While models capture the global mean magnitude of observed warming between 1950-1974 and 2000-2024, they fail to reproduce spatial patterns of temperature change. This limitation…

items.title: Integrated Waste-to-Energy Systems: A comprehensive review of Technologies, decision Frameworks, and sustainability metrics
items.summary_raw: Rising waste generation and growing energy demand have driven global interest in Waste-to-Energy (WtE) systems as a pathway toward sustainable waste management and resource recovery. However, existing WtE reviews remain fragmented: most are technology-centric, focusing on individual conversion routes, while others address environmental performance, economic feasibility, or decision-making methods in isolation, without linking them to waste characteristics or site-specific conditions. This limits the ability of researchers, policymakers, and stakeholders to systematically select suitable WtE solutions for specific regional contexts. This review addresses this gap by first characterizing major waste streams—municipal solid, industrial, agricultural and forestry, sewage sludge, medical, e-waste, and construction and demolition waste—and evaluating their compatibility with thermal (incineration, gasification, pyrolysis), biological (anaerobic digestion, landfill gas recovery), and emerging hybrid conversion technologies. It then examines site-specific factors governing WtE deployment, including economic conditions, geographic and logistical constraints, regulatory and policy drivers, and social acceptance. Building on these dimensions, the review proposes a novel conceptual 3D matrix framework integrating waste type, technology suitability, and site characteristics into a unified selection platform, and synthesizes multi-criteria decision analysis approaches supported by case…

items.title: Assessing biogenic carbon dioxide resource for synthetic e-fuel production to decarbonise shipping
items.summary_raw: A high-level assessment of the production potential and costs of three synthetic e-fuels, methane, methanol and Fischer–Tropsch diesel, derived from renewable hydrogen and biogenic carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) was conducted for maritime transport in the EU and Ireland for 2050. Biogenic CO 2 sources included by-products from biomethane production and ethanol fermentation (priced at €30/tonne), and emissions from biomass combustion (€80/tonne). Direct air carbon capture (€400/tonne) was assessed as a supplementary carbon source. The analysis evaluates CO 2 availability, fuel production potential, hydrogen and electrolysis requirements, and levelised fuel costs relative to projected maritime energy demand of 705 TWh in the EU and 3.86 TWh in Ireland. Based on the assumptions used, total theoretical biogenic CO 2 enables methane and methanol production exceeding projected EU maritime energy demand. In contrast, Fischer–Tropsch diesel production potential from biogenic CO 2 yields only 59% of projected demand, requiring supplementary direct air carbon capture. Methanol recorded the lowest modelled levelised production cost at €113/MWh. Fischer–Tropsch diesel was significantly more expensive (€312/MWh) due to higher hydrogen and CO 2 requirements, lower carbon utilisation and broader product distribution. Biogenic CO 2 availability for the maritime sector may decrease due to competition from other sectors, such as aviation, and limited access to point sources. If the biogenic CO 2…

items.title: Actors and tactics of climate obstruction and governance mechanisms for mitigation and sustainability
items.summary_raw: Global climate action has progressed through public mobilization, scientific consensus, policy commitments, and governmental pledges, yet it is still not adequate to reach set climate targets due to climate obstructionism. The actors of climate obstruction and their strategies and techniques are examined in this state-of-the-art review as a systemic issue influencing public perception, governance, and policy. Leading actors, narratives, strategies, and processes of climate obstruction along with four interrelated domains: corporate, political, bureaucratic, and socio-ideological obstruction, are identified by the investigation. Enhancing transparency procedures, controlling corporate and political interference, promoting independent media and scientific communication, and boosting public resistance to false information are among the highlighted recommendations for better climate actions. For governance, addressing the climate issue necessitates overcoming deliberate and planned obstruction rooted in governance institutions, along with policy design and technical solutions. Despite official promises, climate policy will continue to experience delays, fragmentation, and implementation failure if the coordinated corporate, political, bureaucratic, and socio-ideological opposition entrenched in governance systems is not addressed. Addressing the climate crisis therefore requires not only technological and policy innovations, but also confronting the systemic structures and power…

items.title: Deciding Factors of India’s Foreign Policy
items.source_name: The Paradigm Chronicle Journal of Academic Inquiry and Critical Thought
items.summary_raw: India’s foreign policy has evolved continuously since independence in response to the interaction of domestic priorities, strategic interests, and changes in the international system. This paper examines the major factors that shape India’s foreign policy and influence its engagement with regional and global actors. It highlights geography and historical experience as enduring determinants, while national security, economic interests, energy requirements, technological advancement, domestic politics, political leadership, and public opinion constitute important dynamic influences. Particular attention is given to India’s relations with neighbouring countries, major powers, and multilateral organisations, as well as its growing engagement with the Indo-Pacific, Southeast Asia, and West Asia. The paper also discusses the significance of maritime security, terrorism, nuclear policy, the Indian diaspora, climate change, and global economic interdependence in contemporary foreign-policy formulation. It argues that strategic autonomy remains a central characteristic of India’s external relations, enabling the country to maintain diverse partnerships without becoming permanently aligned with any single power bloc. The study concludes that India’s foreign policy represents a continuing effort to balance national security, economic development, international cooperation, and strategic flexibility in an increasingly complex global order.

items.title: Sustainable Narrative Canvas - Ein Leitfaden zur Erstellung nachhaltiger Produktnarrative
items.source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.summary_raw: DE:Der Sustainable Narrative Canvas ist ein strukturierter Leitfaden, der sich an Designerinnen und Designer richtet, die die Nachhaltigkeit von Produkten und Dienstleistungen über Material und Funktion hinaus gestalten wollen. Zwölf Arbeitsblätter helfen bei der Entwicklung nachhaltigkeitsbezogener Produktnarrative, deren zentrale Erkenntnisse am Ende in einer kompakten Übersicht zusammenlaufen. Das Projekt entstand im Rahmen von SBYD.SPACE an der Folkwang Universität der Künste in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Wuppertal Institut. SBYD.SPACE erforscht klimaneutrale und ressourcenschonende Lebens- und Produktionsweisen und überträgt Wissen aus der Nachhaltigkeitsforschung durch Design in Gesellschaft und Wirtschaft. Weitere Informationen und Materialien unter:https://sbyd.space/projects/sustainable-narrative-canvas/ EN:The Sustainable Narrative Canvas is a structured guide for designers who want to shape the sustainability of products and services beyond material and function. Twelve worksheets support the development of sustainability-related product narratives, whose key findings come together in a concise overview at the end. The project was carried out within SBYD.SPACE at Folkwang University of the Arts in collaboration with the Wuppertal Institute. SBYD.SPACE explores climate-neutral and resource-conserving ways of living and producing and uses design to transfer knowledge from sustainability research into society and the economy.More Information and…

items.title: Traditional or novel plant-based proteins? Consumer preferences and climate policy simulations in China
items.summary_raw: Abstract Plant-based proteins can reduce the carbon footprint of diets, but the relative roles of traditional plant proteins and novel plant-based meat (PBM) remain unclear. We conduct a national online discrete choice experiment (DCE) with 2,161 urban Chinese respondents to compare tofu , a traditional plant protein, and modern PBM as potential substitutes for animal proteins. Mixed logit estimates show that, after controlling for a range of attributes including price, carbon footprint, organic status, and production origin, consumers intrinsically prefer animal protein, followed by PBM and tofu . Latent class results identify four consumer segments—meat lovers, vegetarians, PBM adopters, and indifferent consumers—each with distinct preference rankings and socioeconomic characteristics. Monte Carlo policy simulations show that, despite being less intrinsically preferred than PBM, tofu plays a substantial role in increasing the market share of non-animal proteins due to its price advantage. Moreover, carbon labeling generates larger simulated shifts toward non-animal proteins: the market share increases from 8% in the baseline to 19% under a meat tax and 36% under carbon labeling. Our findings highlight the substantial potential of traditional plant proteins in promoting dietary shifts, and support the use of information-based strategies to reduce carbon emissions from food consumption.

items.title: Contrasting Stances on Sustainability by the USA and China
items.source_name: The Journal of Population and Sustainability
items.summary_raw: As the world’s preeminent greenhouse gas emitters, the United States and China are moving along increasingly divergent sustainability trajectories. Applying a political economy and demographic lens, this article contends that national emission profiles are shaped by a complex interplay of climate threat perceptions, state capacity, energy strategies and shifting attitudes toward multilateralism. While China integrates rapid renewable expansion with persistent fossil fuel reliance under a state-led developmental model, the United States has recently implemented domestic deregulation and withdrawal from international climate accords. Beyond these institutional contrasts, a paradoxical convergence in attitudes toward population growth, despite the nations’ sharply different demographic trends, is identified. Overall, the analysis advances the discourse on climate inequality and the viability of collective global climate action, highlighting how demographic dynamics and political economy jointly determine the prospects for sustainability.

items.title: The future of spatial energy planning: A shift toward social learning and participatory visioning
items.summary_raw: Participatory planning is increasingly used to address complex challenges such as deciding where and how the energy transition should be implemented. Yet it remains unclear what people learn through participatory planning processes and how this learning shapes collective outcomes. This study examines social learning in a participatory regional visioning process in Knonauer Amt, Switzerland. Using surveys conducted before and after the process, we compare changes in the perspectives of participants ( N = 46) with those of non-participating regional residents ( N = 703). Participants' perspectives on spatial planning and the energy transition became more closely aligned than those of the wider regional population, although substantial differences remained. Despite these differences, the process produced a shared regional vision. The findings show that people do not need to agree on everything to move forward together. Participatory visioning can create a shared direction even when differences remain.

items.title: Public knowledge, perceptions and support for climate and health action in Nairobi: a cross-sectional survey with an embedded conjoint experiment
items.summary_raw: Background Public support is important for the adoption, implementation, and sustainability of effective climate action. Evidence suggests that policy instrument characteristics, individual characteristics, and the way in which climate messages are framed can influence public support. Evidence on the effectiveness of different climate message framing, however, is largely limited to high-income countries, with limited research conducted in Sub-Saharan Africa, where the impacts of climate change are particularly severe. This study aims to assess knowledge and perceptions of climate change and health among urban residents in Nairobi and to examine how different message framings influence public support for climate policies. Methods A cross-sectional household survey will be conducted among adults (≥18 years) in Nairobi, Kenya. A sample of approximately 903 participants will be recruited through face-to-face household interviews. The survey will begin with a conjoint experiment consisting of eight paired-choice tasks comparing policy messages that vary across four attributes: climate framing, benefits, scale, and funding source. The survey will then collect information on knowledge of climate change and health, perceptions of climate-related health risks, experience of climate-related weather events, and socio-demographic characteristics. Descriptive statistics and multivariable regression analyses will be conducted to examine factors associated with climate-health knowledge and…

items.title: Strategic ambitions and discursive divergences: China’s belt and road initiative in official and academic narratives
items.summary_raw: The present article seeks to analyse and interpret the discursive construction and strategic orientation of China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). It aims to elucidate how the initiativeis framed within geopolitical, economic, sociocultural, technological, environmental, and institutional contexts, while critically assessing the coherence and divergences between China’s official narratives and academic discourses. In total, 4,413 academic articles and eight official BRI documents published between 2015 and 2023 were examined through lexical and content analysis. The findings reveal both convergences and contrasts in how the initiative is strategically framed and interpreted. Whereas official sources emphasise historical legitimacy, cultural diplomacy, and institutionalised multilateral engagement, the academic literature explicitly addresses practical challenges such as infrastructure-related environmental risks, geopolitical rivalries, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, and uneven economic benefits.

items.title: The Potentials of Biochar Produced by Pyrolysis Using Biowastes
items.source_name: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF APPLIED SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICAL THEORY
items.summary_raw: The rising generation of biowaste from agricultural, municipal, and industrial activities poses significant environmental and waste management challenges. Pyrolysis presents a viable solution by converting biowaste into biochar, bio-oil, and syngas, offering both waste reduction and resource recovery opportunities. This study investigates the influence of key pyrolysis parameters—temperature, heating rate, and residence time—on biochar yield and quality. Findings reveal that slow pyrolysis (300–500°C) with extended residence time optimizes biochar production, while fast and flash pyrolysis (500–1000°C) prioritize bio-oil and syngas yields, respectively. Furthermore, the study highlights biochar’s potential for soil improvement, carbon sequestration, and pollution mitigation. However, challenges such as the absence of standardized guidelines, limited awareness, and inadequate government incentives hinder its large-scale adoption. To overcome these barriers, the study recommends optimizing process conditions, establishing regulatory frameworks, promoting renewable energy applications, and conducting further research on feedstock variability. Additionally, government incentives and public awareness initiatives are essential to enhance adoption. A thorough economic and environmental assessment of large-scale biochar production is necessary to ensure its long-term sustainability. With continued research, policy support, and technological advancements, pyrolysis can significantly…

items.title: Who’s to Blame for the Climate Crisis?
items.summary_raw: Abstract Climate change presents a paradox for moral judgment: its harms are immense and predictable, yet they arise from diffuse collective processes that seem to frustrate attributions of blame. Thus, many believe responsibility can only be coherently understood in forward-looking, structural terms. I argue, however, that a small but powerful group of actors, which I call the “Carbon Axis,” bears responsibility in a thick, backward-looking sense. The standard excuses (e.g., insignificance, ignorance, and lack of intent), which may exculpate some ordinary contributions to harm, afford this group scant moral cover. If anyone is culpable for the climate crisis, the Axis is.

items.title: Signs of compliance: Message framing influences outdoor recreationists' responses to conservation requests
items.summary_raw: Abstract Natural landscapes shared by people and wildlife often rely on signage to guide people towards behaviours that protect nature, where the justification and framing of these requests may influence how people interpret and respond to them. We conducted a factorial vignette experiment with 600 frequent outdoor recreationists living in Scotland, stratified by age, gender and dog ownership, to test the influence of specific sign features on recreationists' intentions to follow three behavioural requests: keeping dogs on leads, staying on designated trails and avoiding sensitive areas, whilst measuring their perceptions of whether they found requests reasonable. We systematically varied requests by highlighting what the majority of other recreationists do (descriptive norms; ‘nine out of ten people do…’) or requesting the appropriate behaviour outright (injunctive norms; ‘please do…’), and by justifying requests for either single‐species conservation, general biodiversity conservation or for self and pet safety. Overall, we found high intentions of recreationists to follow the three behavioural requests, which varied significantly across our experimental conditions and with participant age. The effectiveness of injunctive versus descriptive norms depended on request type: injunctive framing nearly doubled the odds of higher perceived reasonableness and compliance intentions for a proscriptive request to avoid an area, but had no significant effect on prescriptively worded…

items.title: Harnessing renewable energy sources for hydrogen production using artificial intelligence within a circular economy framework
items.summary_raw: The alarming scale of devastation in our environment and the grim picture of the global fuel crisis has spurred the need for sustainable energy alternatives. The hydrogen production from renewable energy sources offers a promising solution to achieve a carbon–neutral energy future in line with UN sustainability development goals. This review explores various renewable energy options like solar, wind, geothermal, and biomass for clean hydrogen production, emphasizing their potential, efficiency, life cycle assessment, and recent technological advancements. It also investigates the applications of artificial intelligence and machine learning in hydrogen production, inspecting the associated challenges and the opportunities available for researchers to pursue further investigations. A bibliometric analysis using the Scopus database and VOS viewer identifies research gaps in this field, putting spotlight on areas such as biomass-based hydrogen production and alternative storage methods. The density maps highlight the less predominant renewable sources as biomass, natural gas (yellow cluster) and fuel cells, electric energy storage (purple cluster) indicating gaps which could be explored by future research enthusiasts. This study further highlights the significance of circular economy principles and role of AI in maximizing resource utilization while minimizing waste. While challenges such as high production costs and infrastructure limitations persist, policy support and…

items.title: Public Communication for the Free Nutritious Meals Program (MBG): Analysis of Public Discourse, Criticism, and Support in West Nusa Tenggara
items.summary_raw: This study aims to analyze the dynamics of public discourse, criticism, and support regarding the Free Nutritious Meals Program (MBG) in the public sphere of West Nusa Tenggara (NTB). The study employs a qualitative approach using a descriptive case study design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with the public, program implementers, and academics, supplemented by observation and documentation. The findings indicate that the MBG narrative is constructed by the government as a strategic program for improving nutrition and equitable welfare, and is subsequently reinterpreted by the public based on their direct experiences. The criticism that emerges is generally constructive and relates to technical aspects of implementation, and is addressed through evaluation and improvements. Community support is evident in social acceptance and active participation in program implementation. This study concludes that the success of the MBG in NTB is significantly influenced by dialogic and participatory public communication in the public sphere.

items.title: Antimicrobial Resistance Under a Changing Climate
items.source_name: Journal of the Royal Society of New Zealand
items.summary_raw: The landscape of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is changing across the animal, human and environmental ecosphere, with both climate change and AMR recognised as leading threats to human health. In this viewpoint, we argue that climate change is likely to reshape the conditions under which AMR emerges, persists and spreads, with important implications for how risks are understood and managed in Aotearoa New Zealand (ANZ). These risks arise because climate-related exposures interact with existing vulnerabilities and adaptive capacity across human, animal and environmental systems. Addressing AMR under climate change requires long-term, transdisciplinary planning that integrates surveillance, infrastructure resilience, emissions reduction and protection of human, animal and environmental systems. We highlight the need for a One Health lens to understand transmission pathways across human, animal and environmental systems, situated within a broader Planetary Health perspective that recognises AMR as part of interconnected challenges of climate change, including pollution and biodiversity loss. Therefore, embedding AMR within climate adaptation health planning is essential to strengthen resilience and reduce future public and environmental health risks.

items.title: Governments must reconcile dissonant climate assessment approaches
items.summary_raw: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02736-4 Security analysts and government economists increasingly present policymakers with different pictures of the same climate and nature risk. We argue that governments need a shared way to weigh these assessments, particularly given that under-preparing for a severe, irreversible outcome costs far more than over-preparing.

items.title: Beyond 2030: what sectoral shifts in EU and China reveal about Long Term climate commitments
items.summary_raw: Abstract The European Union (EU) and China, as two of the largest economies and emitters, play a pivotal role in the global energy transition. While both economies have committed to ambitious decarbonization pledges in the form of Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and Long-Term Targets (LTTs) under the Paris Agreement, the feasibility of their mid-century climate goals remains uncertain. This work employs two leading Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs)—PROMETHEUS and GCAM—to compare the sectoral emissions reductions, final-energy mix, electrification rates and technology mixes associated with NDC–LTT-consistent pathways in the two regions. The study uses a scenario based on the combination of NDCs and LTTs to identify post-2030 sectoral shifts across major economic and emitting sectors. The findings show that China relies on concentrated post-2030 power and industrial decarbonisation, while the EU pathway depends more on sustained fossilfuel exit in end-use sectors. These contrasts point to different implementation risks: China needs early preparation for a compressed post-2030 power–industry transition, whereas the EU needs stronger delivery in residual fossil-fuel use across buildings, transport and industrial heat. By distinguishing robust requirements from model dependent uncertainties, the analysis identifies where future NDCs should move from aggregate pledges to sector-specific roadmaps backed by policy instruments, investment strategies and implementation…

items.title: The role of contextual factors, school-related attitudes and behavioural traits on lifetime antisocial behaviours among adolescents
items.summary_raw: Introduction Antisocial behaviour is a result of a multifactorial process that involves both social-level and individual-level factors. The present study aims to investigate the association of contextual factors with the odds of engaging in antisocial behaviours, and to explore the role of school-related attitudes and behavioural traits in the association between contextual factors and antisocial behaviour among 12- to 14-year-old adolescents. Methods The analytical sample included 1847 students of 29 secondary schools in Italy who participated in the baseline survey of the “GAPUnplugged” study. The associations of sociodemographic characteristics, contextual factors, school-related attitudes and behavioural traits with the odds of adolescent’s antisocial behaviour were estimated through multilevel mixed-effect models. Exploratory indirect association models were performed to test the potential mediation role of school-related attitudes and behavioural traits in the relationship between contextual factors and adolescent’s antisocial behaviour. Results The prevalence of at least one antisocial behaviour lifetime was 61.2%, of two 39% and of three or more antisocial behaviours 21.8%. Among contextual factors, perceived parental permissiveness to use substances, low perceived parental support, low perceived class climate, and perceptions of peer’s cigarette, alcohol and illicit drug use were associated with higher odds of antisocial behaviour. Low pupil’s respect for teacher…

items.title: Earth Day for Future: Framing Environmental Awareness via Youth Climate Activism
items.summary_raw: This news framing analysis investigates five years (2019–2023) of news coverage across three German-speaking countries (Austria, Germany, Switzerland) to find out how journalists connect the environmental awareness event “Earth Day” (ED) to the youth climate movement Fridays for Future (FFF). Drawing on a longitudinal data corpus (N = 559) of news articles from print and online news outlets, articles were coded for the actors they name, the sources they consult, the topics they address (political process, elections, meetings, protest events, digital events, publications) and their narration practices. This study finds that 51% of ED news includes a reference to FFF. They do so by referencing the FFF movement and its figures, printing interviews with FFF activists, and linking ED topics to climate activities by FFF. This linkage follows the movement’s trajectory, rising from 40% of ED coverage in 2019 to 70% in 2021, before receding as FFF consolidates and newer protest actors enter the field. The narration in these texts anchors ED news through FFF to create relevance for contemporary news audiences, a framing device introduced as frame coupling, which shows that frame sponsorship is not confined to organized actors but can be assumed by journalistic routine itself.

items.title: From intention to action: explaining disaster preparedness app adoption through a socio-digital TPB framework in Malaysia
items.summary_raw: The increasing use of digital technologies in the context of disaster risks reduction has opened possibilities to better prepare the community using mobile applications. Nevertheless, the ubiquity of disaster preparedness applications is not necessarily associated with the adoption of such applications and ultimately preparedness behaviour. This paper analyses the drivers of the adoption of disaster preparedness mobile application through a broadened socio-digital Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB). In Malaysia (Penang), a cross-sectional survey was carried out with the residents of two hazard-prone communities (n = 390). Findings on the data were analysed with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) and weighted least squares mean and variance adjusted (WLSMV) estimator. The findings also suggest that the attitude to disaster mobile applications is the best predictor of Behavioural Intention to use respective technologies. Subjective norms and Perceived Behavioural Control (PBC) on the other hand have no significant implications on intention.
